title: The BEST candy EVER!!!
text:
I've tried the rest, but this is the BEST!

I've been eating See's candies since I was just a kid! Easter was one of my favorite holidays, because my mom would order See's large easter eggs, we would get to pick our favorite filling, Chocolate or Chocolate Walnut, then we'd get a medium chocolate egg, I would always choose the Bordeaux (by far the best flavored candy See's sells), you could get the divinity if you liked that. The buttercream is always a huge favorite at our house. You have your choice of Dark or Milk chocolate. Choose your own liking! I prefer Milk chocolate. Another of my favorites is California Brittle. Also, the Vanilla Nut Carmel (no chocolate on this one), but very tasty!

Just remember the Assorted premade box doesn't always have the best picks in it. If you like nuts and chews, that's one of the better choices. I prefer to go down to See's and select my own mix! Pecan turtles--just melt in your mouth. Try the truffles if you like!

Never did like Godiva or Fanny Farmer, once in awhile I could take a piece of Helen Grace or Lindt, but they never live up to my standards.
See's is the perfect candy and it makes the perfect gift for family, friends, co-workers, neighbors, service company's and the postal person. Don't cross anyone off your list until you surprise them with a gift of See's candy for the Holidays.

title: PREMIUM MOBILE CULLINARY ADJUNCT
text:
I purchased this product as a premium-quality, MSG-Free, mobile culinary adjunct, for my various bug-out, camping, and hiking field kits (packs).

When you are exhausted from arduous hiking terrain, or when you are (I can only imagine) in a forced survival or bug-out situation ... Or even if you are stuck at a remote bus-stop, in Winter ... It is just good sense and totally worth it to have PREMIUM BEVERAGE AND SOUP-STOCK (Stew base) OPTIONS, at hand, for the purposes of comfort, morale, and congenial hospitality (sharing with old friends or new acquaintances). So when I am cold and or wet ... feeling down or demoralized ... hungry or thirsty or just showing off ... I like to keep STARBUCKS VIA INSTANT COFFEE and SAVORY CHOICE BEEF AND POULTRY BROTHS, GOURMET HOT CHOCOLATE AND HOT CIDERS AND SPECIALTY HERBAL TEAS (as well as yummy exotic sports and electrolyte cold beverages)IN MY EDC DAY PACK (waist pack or gear-slinger) ... I also carry a Trangia Alcohol Stove (Spirit Burner) or a Cat-Stove with sufficient fuel to boil a gallon or more of water. I even keep a few packets of flavored instant oats and similar snacks.

These premium options do cost more but I consider them to be a luxury and a guilty pleasure, at best, and an essential lift for down spirits, in a bad or uncomfortable situation. WORTH IT ! (and then some).

I wish the Turkey flavored version was similarly priced ... That is my preference but cost way more (My largess does have it's limits).

It is nice to offer an unwitting guest so many delightful options in unexpected places and situations. Sure to please and impress, even if you are just pleasing yourself.

A small spice-shaker with a mixture of garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper or cayenne (etc.) ain't a bad idea, either.
Do not forget to keep a few disposable guest cups handy. They sell disposable coffee cups at your grocer.

Do This ... you are worth it and so are your friends. I keep my surplus in the fridge, to extend the shelf life.

YUMMMMMmmm !

title: Side Benefit -> Workout Getting The Clumps Out
text:
Product: Choco Milk Chocolate Flavored Drink Mix (30% Less Sugar), 14.1 Oz

I got this because of the 30% less sugar. I didn’t have another can of chocolate mix sitting around to compare, but I’ll take their word on it. From the label’s nutritional info, it’s probably about right. It’s not overly sweet in taste. That’s fine with me, but if you like really sweet chocolate milk, this may not be for you. It’s also very light on the chocolate flavor. That one is not so okay for me. I really wanted more chocolate flavor than this delivers.

Even for a chocolate milk mix, this clumps horribly. Prepare for a workout trying to get as many clumps out as possible. Don’t think about getting them all out. I took a whisk to it and there were still lumps in the milk. I’ve taken to adding a spoonful of it to my coffee. The hot liquid helps it dissolve a bit better, but there is still a fair amount in the bottom of the cup not dissolved. It might work to use it in baking, but I’ve been hesitant to try because of the possibility it would just clump in that as well.

This is a product of Mexico. It was properly sealed and the expiration date was good for a little over a year. The canister says to use it by a month after opening it. It won’t get used in that time for me, but I suspect it will still be okay.

Less sugar: positive. Clumping and weak flavor: negative. I ended up feeling this was just an average product, and one I probably wouldn’t get again.

title: SmokyBeast Review: Ardbeg Uigeadail - Holy Smoke!
text:
SmokyBeast dot com review (tune in for weekly reviews of your favorite Islay malts!)

Follow the southern coast of Islay from Port Ellen heading west, and you will pass, in this order, Laphroaig, Lagavulin, and then Ardbeg. At the north end of this legendary isle are beastly distilleries like Caol Ila, Bowmore, and Bruichladdich. So with the richest scotch neighbors in the world, it's quite a bold statement for Ardbeg to claim its title as "The Peatiest and Smokiest of all the Islay malts."

But in our experience, it's not just about being the smokiest or the peatiest. It's about the balance of the whisky. The beauty of beasts like Lagavulin and Caol Ila is that they use the smoke and peat flavor to counter the alcohol to achieve amazing smoothness, bringing out all the sweet and unique flavors of the malt.

"Uigeadail" literally means "dark and mysterious" and its namesake is Loch Uigeadail, the enigmatic spring from which Ardbeg's water originates. Uigaedail is a limited release Ardbeg that mixes their standard ten year whisky with an older malt that has been aged in sherry casks. Sherry cask-aging has been a big hit in our book so far, so we were excited to taste this Ardbeg.

For Christ's sake, it says "The Ultimate Islay Single Malt Scotch Whisky" right on the bottle. One thing the folks at Ardbeg don't seem to suffer from is modesty. But hey, fortune favors the bold, so let's jump in and see how it measures up.

The Ardbeg Line
The standard Ardbeg bottle is the 10-Year, which is available from KL for $42.99. They also make the "Corryvreckan" at $73.99 which they describe as "black tarry expresso coffee that coats the palate with rich melted dark fruits". Rounding out the lineup is the Supernova - which has not been available since 2010 - which is pumped up to a ridongculous peat level of 100 parts per million and was around $130. The Uigeadail is avaialble from KLwines for $58.99 for a limited time. There is also a "Blasda" bottle which "removes some of the peat" - i.e. it's an Ardbeg for the faint of heart and doesn't merit further discussion. Removing the peat from Ardbeg would be like removing the sport from a Ferrari.

Tasting Notes

Nose: "It smells like I'm on the island of Islay standing next to a smoking heap of peat!" "Grapefruit, honey, hot pepper." Very intriguing nose sets up high levels of anticipation for the first sip.

Body (neat): Amazingly smooth for the high alcohol content. Deep rich smoke, multiple layers of peat. Very rich milk chocolate mocha. Wow, can this really be 54.2%?? It's far and away the smoothest high-test whisky we've ever tasted.

Finish: Sweet candy (salt water taffy?), black licorice, even more layers of peat smoke. Very little burn, the heavy alcohol content is covered almost completely by the serious smoke. And at the very end, just a tiny hint of raisins reminiscent of the sherry cask.

Second taste (with a dose of water - more than a drop, less than a splash) - Opens up with more of the grapefruit and hot red pepper. Amazingly smooth now, actually all it needs is a few drops. Keeping it's body and strength through a splash of water, or a single small ice cube, this is an immensely drinkable dram.

Review
Our only concern in writing this review is how we're going to keep finding whiskies that measure up to the fantastic experiences we've been having the past few months. At under $60, the Ardbeg Uigeadail is just not even fair. We're giving it an "A". Never mind that you're getting ten percent more booze in this bottle. Never mind that it's basically a cask-strength whisky that's so smooth you can drink it straight. Just let your first sip linger on your tongue, let the rich Islay breeze and the peat smoke rise through your nose to the top of your head, sit back relax and enjoy the ride. Pick up a bottle (or a case) of this beauty. At this price and quality it will go fast.

title: Sending a Hug
text:
Some of my friends do not live close to me anymore, and I miss them.  Sending a gift like this lets you feel like you are sharing a cup of tea with them.

This package includes five hand-chosen items, which are :
- A box of Cup of Love Tea - 
- Dried Flowers
- Pearl Sheet Face Mask
- Raspberry Jam Petites Cookies 
- Sea Salt + Sage, Soy Candle

My favorite part of this box was the raspberry jam shortbread cookies. A larger pack of these cookies should coincide with the amount of tea bags.

My least favorite part of this gift set was the pressed dried flowers and the candle. 
The flowers and candle seemed unnecessary as they did not fit with the theme of this gift.

If I were personally designing this basket, then I would have made several changes.

For example, the cookies should not have been miniature since they looked like a toy you would find at a child’s tea party.

The pressed dried floral arrangement and candle are two items that I felt were unnecessary.

A floral-scented candle would have been the perfect compliment to this set. Also, I would have preferred a different greeting card style since the enclosed card resembles an inexpensive postcard.

The sturdy packaging is a welcome keepsake after you finish using all the goodies. You can see it was hand-wrapped, which gives it that unique personal touch.

title: Why pay the price of a bottle of vodka for flavored water.
text:
I used to drink beverages containing alcohol. I no longer do so.
Although working with " heritage herbs and or spices" is highly commendable, the resulting product is lacking in flavor.
Perhaps the price of the product is justified by the painstaking task of small batch distillation. But it is water.
That this product could be used as a mixer is utter nonsense. Even the introduction of an ice cube is out of the question. Tonic water? Absolutely not, unless you enjoy the taste of quinine that has been mildly altered.
Save your money. A much more palatable choice is Number 1 Rosemary Water (sparkling). I applaud the attempt. Keep trying Seedlip. This is a great idea that has not realized it's potential.

title: THIS IS GOOD STUFF!
text:
We loved this Salt and Vinegar Wing Dust. I had tried to recreate S&V wings at home with a few convoluted recipes I found online with little luck and finally searched on Amazon for a powder in Amazon Grocery and found this stuff. It was the hit of our Barbecue Wing Fry this Labor Day Weekend. We cooked up dozens of wings up nice and crispy in a turkey fryer and tried various sauces as well as this S&V dust, and it was a HIT. I put some in a recycled garlic powder shaker and sprinkled the dust on the wings so as not to waste this precious stuff. If you like Salt and Vinegar, THIS IS GOOD STUFF!

Edited to add that even though we re-sealed the bag well, moisture got in and ruined the product. Maybe if it came in smaller bags? I will buy again but I will put the remaining in a glass jar with a tight lid and add some desiccant packs.

title: If you like chickpea puffs you will love these snacks
text: I’ve been buying white cheddar chickpea puffs from a local warehouse store for quite some time so I was somewhat anxious to try these. I wasn’t disappointed. With regard to texture, these puffs are actually a little lighter (more puffier?) than what we have been buying. I put all three flavors out last night when we had friends over. Some people didn’t care for them because they don’t like chickpeas or the texture. However, everyone who likes chickpeas really enjoyed them. The chickpea puffs are very flavorful. In fact, the white cheddar version has more flavor than those we buy at the local warehouse store.  The favorite for most people last night was the ranch flavor. These puffs provide a burst of ranch flavor that’s great. I don’t like spicy food so the after taste from the blazin’ hot flavor was too much for me. However, friends who love spice really liked them. Bottom line, if you like chickpea puffs these have excellent texture and flavor.

title: This starter is awesome
text:
It took a little while to arrive , but the wait was well worth it.
There's probably enough starter in this package to do 100-150 batches.

I had a firm dense mass within 26 hours after inoculation.

I used 4 cups of dried soy beans after soaking and cooking mixed 2 Tablespoons of rice wine vinegar and 2 teaspoons of the tempeh starter.

I split the batch between two 6" X 8" Pyrex dishes, and put them in my fermentation station preheated to 95 degrees. 9 hours later the fungus was very active, as the tempeh cakes were generating their own heat, and peaked out around 113 degrees.

This went really well, and I already have a batch of lentils, brown rice, sunflower seeds and pumpkin seeds soaking to start tomorrow.

title: High quality 24K gold, makes awesome drinks
text:
I used Barnabas Gold flakes (both in the bottle and the sheets) for gold martinis for my Oscar party. The product and the vendor are awesome. They were very nice to answer any questions I had regarding making ice cubes and martinis with the gold and even tested it for me.

I used the gold in three ways:

1. free floating flakes (the easiest way to do this is to use their sheet in a bottle and follow their directions with by mixing a little alcohol with water in their provided small bottle, shake, then put into drink.) If you have your own small bottle you can buy more of their sheets insert a sheet, and follow same directions. But if this is your first time mixing gold in drinks I would just buy their bottle, all ready to go. Their one sheet bottle for a 1 liter alcohol bottle or martini pitcher.
2. Ice cubes: I used both large sphere ice cubes with gold (but you need a lot more gold to do these large drink ice cubes) plus the small ice cube trays. For the latter, fill it up halfway, freeze, then insert gold, then mix in rest of water. That way gold stays in cube vs. just floating to the top. You can make the ice cubes, half water, half alcohol but alcohol does not freeze in a regular freezer (the alcohol did freeze for me as I mixed it with water.)
3. I put one small "gold" ice cube in each drink and large sphere ice cubes with gold in it in a clear martini pitcher, offering people a choice of stirred martinis or shaken martinis. Also had gold flakes in the martini shaker so they poured out beautifully into the drink when shaken.

One recommendation to work with it:
1. gold flakes easily: if you use the bottle and mix in alcohol/water, its easy, just shake and put in your larger drink container
2. if you buy the sheets, use at tweezer to gently pick off gold. But if your tweezer gets wet and then sheet gets wet then the gold becomes stuck to sheet. So use a tweezer but keep it dry. I found the combination of a tweezer and a chopstick worked best.

Everyone was awed by these gold martinis. I attached some pictures of the drinks and ice cubes with the gold. The gold is completely edible, does not taste like anything and gives your drinks that special wow factor.

This is a very high quality product: it is real 24 gold I have had some leftover in the bottle, a week has gone by and it has not tarnished, disintegrated or discolored. It looks the same as when I first mixed it. This is REAL 24K gold.

I highly recommend this 24K gold. High quality product. Next year plan to buy more gold and get even more creative with it.

title: Very delicious, useful and somewhat healthier chewing gum.
text:
First off, this gum is not for everybody so you might want to think really hard before buying an entire box of this product. It has been at least 7 years since I've chewed this type of gum. They were either no longer in the health food stores or was so overpriced, it just wasn't worth getting anymore. Not at $4.50 per pack.

This gum has a sweet but an annoying powerful ginseng scent as soon and you open the pack of 20 pieces. The flavor of the gum does not last that long so you may go thru a pack or two before you feel a sense of satisfaction. It gives you a natural boost of energy. It won't make you bounce off the walls but it will help give you a energy boost and little edge in physically demanding activities.

The gum, to me was very delicious and very immersive. I find it that after I chew this gum, it does not insanely affect the taste of foods I eat. Other chewing gums have xylitol and other menthol-cated chemicals that force you to wait 30 minutes before you eat. Otherwise, your food will taste like chewing gum or just make it taste horrible to you.

Only problems I had was; as soon as you open the box, an intense ginseng smell fills the room. If your going to buy this, make sure you open the pack, take what you want out and then seal it in a Tupperware container. The smell can be a nuisance. It good to smell that somewhat, but not all the time. It might make your breath smell a little weird after chewing for some people.

The second thing was the nutritional facts on the package. It doesn't really tell you everything that's in it once you get it translated to a language you can understand unless you speak Russian, Korean, or Spanish. It could be everything but it seems to be missing information. All it says is that it has ginseng power/extract, sugar, your usual gum base, carbohydrates(that is practically sugar too)... Not much else. I dont know if there is any iron or other ingredients that could be in it. Reasearch turned up useless. The amount of sugar that's in it seems to balance out the ginseng flavor so that it's not too bitter but not too sweet. But more sugar than ginseng according to the taste.

I would not recommend using this as a dietary supplement, if you have diabetes, or overweight. Chew this in moderation. Put it in your lunch bag, pantry, purse, or in your pocket whenever you are on the go. The gum taste great to me. There shouldn't be any harm in trying it.

Packaging was perfect. Air pocket-, thingys worked well and kept the package unharmed and in tact.

title: great coffee, poor k-cup design
text:
Taste is very subjective, so reviewing a food or beverage based on taste can be difficult. Personally, I enjoy the taste of this coffee and it is now my "go to" dark roast. This is a dark, smooth, and bold roast. Gevalia is a Swedish company, so their coffee tends to be darker and bolder, which is favored in Scandinavia and Northern Europe.

*IMPORTANT NOTE*
Keurig's patents on the K-Cup capsule design expired in 2012, which unfortunately flooded the market with generic K-Cup capsule designs. Gevalia uses one of these generic designs which has a slightly different shape and has ridges on the sides. Unfortunately, as many other reviewers have pointed out, this capsule design does not seem to work well in Keurig brewers. However, there is a simple fix for this problem which should work every time: When you put the Gevalia K-Cup in the brewer, push it down to manually puncture the bottom, then close the top and brew like normal.

title: Fantastic product...for some people.
text:
I would imagine that this product is not for everyone. If you're the sort of person to intentionally dilute your whisky by about 20% to tease out the more subtle flavors, or if you insist on your gin martini being stirred gently rather than shaken, then you may well enjoy Seedlip. (Note that while I'm using alcohol to make a point, these in no way replicate the taste or mouthfeel of alcohol. If that is your hope, prepare to be disappointed.)

On the other hand, if you think the best way to drink something is ice cold and full strength, then you will probably be disappointed. The taste is there, and it is strong and to my mind pleasant, but I can easily imagine some of my friends who proudly drink high proof scotch that tastes like a firepit straight from the bottle as being underwhelmed, both due to their palate sensitivity being dialed way down, and due to their expectations.

My father said he could barely taste anything...but he over salts literally everything, and seems to be able to taste only the most aggressive of seasonings. My wife found the botanicals a little overwhelming, but she has a much more sensitive palate than myself. (She did enjoy them diluted in a proper cocktail.)

I have enjoyed each of them so much that I ordered another set of bottles directly from Seedlip without even finishing my first set. So, if you have a reasonably sensitive palate, you enjoy taste profiles that include heavy herbal and bitter notes, and you tend to savor a complex drink, then I'd say give it a try. They have improved literally every drink I've mixed them into.

title: Godsend for Peanut Butter Addicts
text:
I read that the high omega-6 fat in peanuts is not good for your body, which is bad news for peanut butter lovers like me. This peanut flour cuts most of the fat out. By mixing it with a little water or almond milk you can make a peanut butter spread that is high in protein and low in carbs, but doesn't have a ton of fat in it. You can even thin it out to make more of a sauce consistency for dipping fruit. Keep in mind it doesn't have any added sugar, and most regular PB does. So I recommend adding a little spoonful of Truvia or your favorite sweetener. Makes it taste less weird. It also does not have added salt, but I feel like it doesn't need it. You can also make cookies with it, although I haven't tried that yet. It's also a really good price compared with PB2 and has even less fat.

The main downside is the packaging. I almost feel like a clumsy person in an infomercial trying to cut the package open. By the time I am done it looks like a 5-year-old Freddy got to it. There is no built-in way to reseal it, and the flour loves to puff out of it when you close it. Would be nice to just put this in a resealable bag.

title: Wonderful Array of Flavors
text: While normally orange is high note flavor and cranberry sits on the lower end of the spectrum, this tea mix does an amazing job reversing the roles. The orange takes a deeper background seat to the strong tone of the cranberry. It has a particular tartness to it that will quickly become addicting. As far as dosing, you can get away with 2 tablespoons (6 teaspoons) for about 40 oz.(5 cups) if you let it steep for about 20 minutes. I find this method ideal as the increased steep time allows the orange to come out a bit more...otherwise it gets lost in the cranberry if you infuse too quickly with a greater quantity. Enjoy!

title: Nice, full-bodied, mellow honey
text:
Love the mellow, well-balanced taste of this honey. With its neutral flavor, it works well for everything from toast-topping to tea-sweetener. But like other reviewers have mentioned, it arrived with the top of the cap broken off. As it's sealed inside, it didn't cause leakage during transit, but it's a bit of a bugger trying to get the cap back on, so I put store it in a plastic baggie for added protection.

I cringed a bit at the "Made by American Bees" statement on the label. I'm happy to support American industry with my purchases, but I can do without the nationalistic marketing nonsense. "American bees" collect from plants possibly tainted by glyphosate, if that's something important to you. As Mexico has just banned glyphosate, I don't know that "American bees" (long may they thrive) can be claimed to produce a superior product. But this honey does taste good! I also buy a much larger vat of very good creamed honey from North Dakota, and though I don't know the natural traveling range of bees, personally, I have no problem if they take a little foraging buzz north of the border to Canada (where, sadly, glyphosate is the most commonly used herbicide). But, despite buying mostly organic products, I'm sure I've already got plenty of glyphosate, PFOAs, etc., already in my system, so when it comes to honey, I just go for the flavor!

text: My mother in law bought this kit for my three year old son for Christmas. I looked at the reviews on here and my heart sank. I certainly don't want to imply that the users who rated this one star didn't follow the directions, they may have, but I think it is VITAL to make sure you knead the frosting packet for several minutes to warm it up and get it to a good smooth consistency. Also, make sure you follow the directions regarding how big to cut the opening in the frosting packet (1/4 of an inch I believe). We had no trouble at all getting the pieces of the house to stick together! My only negative complaint was that it was a bit messy getting the sprinkles and other small pieces of candy on to the house and not on our floor/table, but that was part of the fun! title: Excellent product!
text:
Excellent authentic butter that we use for ghee. In our culture, this its considered best to churn buttermilk and extract butter just as Organic Valley does. Folks - You can taste and feel the difference.
Wish I had found it sooner. Knowing it's organic and without GMO also means a lot for me as I care about my family's nutrition.

Suggestions:
**************
1. I would urge Organic Valley to pursue higher level of humae treatment for the cows. Although, you do have a relatively high score in the market, it would certainly help consumers such as myself purchase guilt free.
https://www.cornucopia.org/scorecard/dairy/

2. Also urge you to consider and STOP:
- Artificial insemination
- Painful Dehorning of animals
- Branding cattle without any anesthesia/pain meds.
- Separating the calves immediately from the mother.
- Killing the cows if milk production is lower than expected.
- Killing male calves for meat

I'm fully aware of the cost implications this would translate to, but I'm sure there is a market where we're willing to pay significantly higher cost if these considerations are met.

For an empire like organic valley, this could very will be an exclusive separate arm that caters to this market (which is expanding).

I request you to take this feedback and do your best.

It is never right to separate a child from it's mother, even in the world of animals.

The butter and buttermilk are truly enjoyable. We hope to see some further action taken and would love to purchase more products guilt free!

title: Tastes like paper with a hint of sugar and difficult to cut
text:
I had high hopes for this product on a home made cake.
The product arrives in a clear plastic sleeve with a construction paper graphic around it with instructions on how to apply it.
I peeled the graphics off the plastic backer as the instructions said, and applied them to the cake.
They come off as a semi-flexible material that seems like a cross between rubber and paper to the feel. Easy to cut or tear.
I was nervous putting it on because it seemed too stiff, and tasted like paper.
I was hoping that sitting on the cake would moisten it and make it softer.. but it didn't.
I had to poke it with a knife to get a candle through it.
Cutting it was not easy. It cuts like a piece of construction paper. Sounds like cutting paper too as you saw through it.

Maybe we got an old stale one.. (There is no expiration date on the packaging)
If this is the normal product, I would not recommend these if you actually plan on eating them.
The cake had fresh Buttercream icing on it that was made from scratch just a few minutes before applying the graphic, so the frosting was still plenty moist. The cake was sliced 6-7 hours later.

title: The secret ingredient to high, fluffy, great-tasting biscuits
text:
I've been using Bakewell Cream for 30 years. Yes, it makes better, fluffier biscuits than Rumsford, so ignore that "answer" above. And what's more, and the reason I use it, is that you don't get that tinny flavor from Bakewell Cream that you get from Rumsford and other baking powders. That is the main reason I started using it (I'm a supertaster) and the reason I'll never go back.

To novice Bakewell Cream users, you use Bakewell Cream plus baking soda in, for example, biscuits and they turn out great.

There are a couple of tricks. Their biscuit recipe is aces, you can use it with a couple of modifications, both to do with the liquid (type and amount). The recipe calls for 1 1/2 c milk. Use 1 3/4 c of buttermilk. (Or, halved, use 7/8 c of buttermilk.) Soured milk will work too but I prefer buttermilk. I also prefer a very wet/soft dough. With 1/2" thick dough I will get 2-3" biscuits. It's kind of amazing.

Another thing that may confuse novice users is that you preheat the oven to a high heat (475), bake for 5 minutes, then turn the oven off and let the biscuits remain in the closed oven for 5-7 more minutes. You will think this is not enough time, You will be wrong. 7 minutes in my oven is actually a little bit too long so I err on the side of 5-6 minutes.

Give it a try. If you're getting flat biscuits, it's because you're doing it wrong, basically.

title: Fun!  Fun!  Fun!
text:
What a delight! Three unique hot sauces of varying intensity, starting with a medium verde (green) up to a hot red and a hotter red. It took a few minutes for the third one to wear off my tongue after first tasting. I'm not sure I yet appreciate the flavor the hops bring, but I love the innovation and look forward to learning. It's so fun to add to my otherwise grocery store collection (see picture of 7 bottles), with these extending the heat range (based on Scoville ratings, for the hot sauce fans out there). The Alchemy verde is hotter than the Herdez verde and probably the same intensity as the Cholula or Tapatio red. The Alchemy reds are hotter.

This would be an outstanding gift for a hot sauce fan, but it feels a little pricey. It feels like a great $25 (maybe $30) product.

The box is gift quality, though mine arrived marked up, so a plastic wrapping would help. It would also benefit from an included brochure of Alchemy hot sauces (not other products), especially if the Hopp series is one of several hot sauce series from Alchemy. Even if it's a one-off series, a small brochure with history of pepper cultivation and hot sauce , background on Scoville scale, and the unique Alchemy series would enhance the product nicely.

Nonetheless, I'm excited to add this to my hot sauce collection. I rearranged the corner bin in the refrigerator door so I can find the perfect hot sauce when I need it!

On the plus side, as a spiced cola it did taste good. It has lower calories, lower sugar than normal cola, and uses what appears to be natural ingredients.

Overall, if you're looking for an alcoholic replacement, this is not for you. If you're looking for an expensive spiced, lower calorie, cola drink, then this would be something to try.

title: reheat them to regain the chewy consistency
text: I initially cooked them as directed by boiling them.  The directions say to boil for 5 minutes but many reviewers suggested boiling for longer which I did for 8 minutes.  After straining them, I rinsed with cold water and soaked them in a simple syrup of water, brown and white sugars.  I served a few drinks right away and they were perfect, chewy and soft.  A few hours later, I went back to sample them and they were hard and chalky in the middle, just like other reviewers said they would turn if you didn't use them right away.  Just on a whim, I put some in the microwave.  Guess what?!  They returned to their chewy yumminess!  I was hoping that I could cook the bag and reserve them to use over a few days so I was really disappointed when they turned hard.  A whole bag would've been wasted had I not recooked them.  YAY!!!  Problem solved. :)

title: A quality pumpkin seed oil that brings me back to my childhood.
text:
I grew up using pumpkin seed oil on my salad every since I was very young. My grandfather used to bring it back every time he went on trips to Europe. He used to purchase it from a small company in Slovenia and I've never been able to find anything even CLOSE to that pumpkin seed oil.

On a whim, I found this styrian pumpkin seed oil and decided to give it a try. The package was just as it was pictured, the oil was thick and a rich dark green and the taste was just as I remember-- subtle and nutty. If you have not tried pumpkin seed oil before, I HIGHLY recommend it. The price is worth it and the quality is unmatched.

I use it in a salad with this recipe: romaine lettuce (or whatever lettuce of your choosing), olive oil, vegeta (a group of spices), red wine vinegar, freshly minced garlic, and salt. It is amazing.

title: Nice product, Very Versatile
text:
I like to make my own soups and dips. I own a dehydrator and often dry my own veggies for those uses but honestly, it takes a LOT of fresh veggies and herbs to make the amount of a mix you get with this product! So I feel that it is a good value at $12.95.

I like the fact that this product is pure vegetable and herb. No fillers, No MSG, no weird preservatives I can't pronounce. A silica preserving packet is included in the container. The caloric content is 58 calories per 1/4 cup dry product. 0 fat and cholesterol and only 49 mg of sodium per serving. Ingredients as listed in order on the label: Dehydrated carrots, Onion, tomatoes, peas, celery, green bell peppers, green beans and parsley.

This makes a nice soup base with water but I prefer to use chicken or vegetable broth. I also like to reconstitute the mix and add it to whipped cream cheese or greek yogurt for a nice dip. I also reconstitute and add it to scrambled eggs! It is great added to your meatloaf or hamburger mixtures too. Some uses do call for it to be rehydrated but there are other uses that benefit from the crunchiness of the dehydrated form. Put some in your coffee grinder (I have one that is used exclusively for herb and spice grinding) for a powdery version. If you have a large pepper mill you can put it in there and grind a nice veggie seasoning on anything as you would with pepper! There are many uses for this product and I am enjoying getting creative with it.

I recommend this vegetable "soup" mix. I wish they would rename it Vegetable "EVERYTHING" Mix.

To my surprise, I don't care for the flavor and didn't find it warm or mustardy, but this is just personal preference. To me, it tastes more like something slightly unripe or green.

title: Better than corn tortilla chips!
text:
I am allergic to corn. It did not bother me when I was a kid, but I think that something that is added to genetically modified crops does not agree with my gastrointestinal system. Once I figured this out, I thought I would never get to enjoy tortilla chips or other corn-based snacks again.

That's why I am so excited about these chips. I get to enjoy the crunchy, salty pleasure of tortilla chips and dip, without the discomfort caused by traditional corn products. What's even better is that the beans and rice these chips are made of provide a healthful serving of complete protein, so I can indulge my snack cravings without guilt!

I must say, however, that it is not a good idea to eat too much of these chips. Pour some into a cereal bowl and put the rest away, or share with a friend. Otherwise you will overeat, because they are so good! You may suffer gas, bloating and other discomforts if you eat too much, just as you would if you ate more than your share of Navy beans or chili. Try some of these with your favorite salsa, queso, or guacamole. If you are like me, you won't ever want corn chips again!

title: Whole Cloves Have Underlying Vinegary Odor
text:
The Amazon Happy Belly brand usually offers good value for the price, but the quality isn’t 100 percent consistent. (For example, I’ve experienced considerable variation in quality and freshness of Happy Belly cashew nuts, although they’re a bargain even when the quality isn’t great). Unfortunately, these HAPPY BELLY WHOLE CLOVES (2 Ounces) seem to be one of the poorer quality Happy Belly products.

When I opened the jar, I found that the cloves had a distinctly vinegary odor underlying the expected intense, strong and sweet aroma of cloves. When I compared the aroma to that of a long-ago-opened jar of Spice Island whole cloves, the latter did NOT have the vinegary odor.

My guess is that the vinegary odor has something to do with the cultivation of the Happy Belly cloves. That is, where the cloves were grown, what (if any) fertilizers were used, and what the weather conditions were like during the growing season. It’s very unlikely that the Happy Belly whole cloves were “gone bad”, because whole spices generally last for a couple of years, and only lose strength as they age.

Still, I don’t like the Happy Belly cloves. I will be sticking with the more expensive Spice Islands brand.

title: Makes excellent easy chai lattes!
text:
Of course, taste is subjective, but I find this to be a very good chai tea. I bought a box of 100 to go with the milk frother (BonJour Cafe Monet Manual Frother) I bought at the same time, and with the two, and maybe a bit of Italian vanilla syrup, it's easy to make very tasty chai lattes. (The frother actually works best with 0% or 1% milk and still makes an extremely rich froth, so even a large tea isn't calorie intensive.) As regular chai tea it's fine too, but the lattes are SO easy and SO good that's what we always end up making.

For a large mug, more than about 14 ounces, I use two tea bags because I prefer it fairly strong, but otherwise a single bag is fine. The pack of 100 arrives in a standard cardboard box, no fancy packaging, but the individual tea bags are the foil type, so I assume they'll stay fresh for a long time.

Bottom, line, especially if using a milk frother, this product makes for an excellent chai tea or chai tea latte, equal to any you might pay $4 or $5 for at you-know-where. (And I highly recommend the BonJour frother too, which, come to think of it, would make a great gift combination.)

title: Good value
text:
We’ve used various brands of Himalayan pink salt over the years. We have tended to avoid the very fine grinds because they can be almost like a dusty powder.

This fine grind is very much like table salt in size of grains. I think it’s going to be useful both in salt shakers, and in the salt box we keep next to the cook top.

The color in this batch is very light pink, but it’s always varied from batch to batch in the various brands we’ve used in the past. The taste is the same as other pink salt, and if you use pink salt, you know it’s far different than white table salt, which tastes harsh and almost chemical by comparison.

The main reason I switched to this supplier was the much lower price, and the guarantee that it is 100% Himalayan pink salt.

It arrived packed well, and there was only a tiny pinhole in one bag that I easily sealed with a piece of packaging tape.

I would recommend this seller and their product. We will purchase again from them.

title: Hard to Describe How Much Better These Are
text: I'm not a huge fan of Vienna Sausages, but my mother is, so I found these on sale the other day and bought a couple of cases. I decided to try them and was blown away by how much better they are than regular Vienna Sausages. First the texture of the smoked sausages is quite different. They are firmer and the smoking process creates and almost "crust" like effect on the exterior of the individual pieces giving them a little desperately needed "bite". The smoke flavor is just what the normally bland sausages needed. It takes something that had very little flavor and adds just the note necessary to really perk them up. If you like Vienna Sausages give these a try. If you normally don't care for them, find a single can in the store and see what you think. These are great camping food, a lite lunch with a few crackers in the briefcase or a quick snack at home.

Yes it’s true that homemade almost always tastes better than processed, but I was expecting only minor inconsistencies. It tasted old and it was really grainy. It does, however, cook things perfectly well and can reach high temps without smoking. If I ever purchase more ghee from different brands and find they all taste the same, I will change my review. title: Cheap, artificial and insipid.
text:
Packaging was attractive and fun. That’s it.

Everything else seems like corners were cut for the consumer to make it as cheap as possible. Given that syrup is a cheap product with lots of room for profit, that’s really saying something.

Bottle quality: Some of the bottles leaked from the top, despite having a plastic seal that you need a knife to wrest off. That’s because someone opted to get a wrapping around the top that stretches but doesn’t tear without a knife or a sharpened guitarists fingernail.

But let’s suppose you get the wrapping off and cleaned up the leaked syrup. At least now you can enjoy the rewards of your labor. Right? Think again.

The flavors are all artificial and taste like plastic or some chemical was mixed in with the syrup. I suppose that’s the sweetener which paradoxically doesn’t taste all that sweet.

Any semblance of the labeled flavor is quite bland and won’t stand up to coffee—supposing you don’t mind the chemical flavor that predominates. Pumpkin spice and French Vanilla have a similar smell of acrid pepper. Was French vanilla spiced?

Sticking with the MONIN syrups I would usually get.

For those who may be curious, they’re also all labeled ‘made in China.’

title: Less might be more with this product.
text:
Well, I have 'pre-diabetes' and started a low-carb diet. It's been difficult, especially as my husband is along for the ride. We both have a sweet tooth and I wanted something I could bake with so I tried this product. When I use it more sparingly I like it. When I use it as a sugar substitute and increase the amount of this to match what is supposed to be the sweetness of sugar, I do not like it as much and get the 'cooling' sensation others have mentioned.

At first I used it sparingly, in a coconut flour pancake recipe. As I had sugar free syrup and did not want them sweet enough to stand on its own I used less than the recipe called for. No cooling sensation. Nothing offensive.

I used in it a basic baked egg custard last night with eggs, heavy cream, almond milk, and vanilla. Nothing else. The recipe called for 1/2 a cup sugar, so to keep with the claims that it is 70% as sweet, I used over 1/2 cups of this. The custard cooked and set beautifully, as others have noted. The experience of eating was a bit rocky though. The first few bites were quite good. By the end though, I had a tingling in my mouth, a cool sensation and a weird feeling in my throat. Not so good. It should be noted that, my husband did not have the same experience.

I was left a bit disappointed. But I am not throwing in the towel on it yet. I am going to go with the assumption that less is more and test it to see if I can tolerate it using it in certain recipes.

ETA: I used it again. And this time I am using a 1:1 ratio and really being careful about my recipes. It is much better in a 1 to 1 ratio. I can handle a little cooling. But using more than 1:1 gives it too much to tolerate.

The stems are very fibrous and no amount of soaking will make them easy to chew.
I cooked all the moisture out of them after soak, with garlic, shallots and salt I didn't want to over power the flavor. These absorb flavors nicely. Oddly, they are described as tasting a bit like oyster but I didn't think so. Maybe if they are fresh they do.

Overall, I'm sold. A new fan of oyster mushrooms. Delicious!

title: Nice addition to my daily smoothie with health benefits
text:
Non-GMO and Vegan? Yes please.
Middle age woes....added this to potentially help reduce joint inflammation, improve cholesterol levels, blood glucose stabilization and immune response (among other benefits).
I make a daily smoothie for lunch filled with an assortment of fruits, greens, omegas and almond milk. One thing missing? This product.
Day 1: over-jealous! TWO scoops (they provide a very small scoop in container) into my daily smoothie.....overpowering taste, indigestion and unsettled tummy.
Day 2: Reduced to 1 Scoop. Same issues as day 1
Day 3: Reduced to 1/2 scoop and perfect!
-Stayed at 1/2 scoop for a week.
-Gradually increased the amount into my smoothie over the course of a month.
-I’m now using 2 scoops without any side effects (I make a double batch smoothie. One for today and one for the next day).
My recommendation for those naive to this or similar products is to begin slowly and increase gradually.
The taste is pleasant (albeit semi strong when first incorporating into my smoothie). Would describe the taste similar to a chai tea or latte but, a tad more intense. But, gradually incorporated, my taste buds adapted.
Have not had a decrease in joint pain. But, hoping this helps improve cholesterol, blood glucose levels (they’ve been out of range for years after chemo) and immune response over time. My skin looks and feels semi-better...not sure if this product is helping in this area?

title: Cocozia is wonderful
text:
We were asked to review Cocozia coconut water and were happy to oblige. We have tried a lot of coconut water brands in the marketplace so we felt confident with providing a fair and accurate review of Cocozia.

First off, here's what we look for when choosing a coconut water:

•level of sweetness
•after-taste
•pasteurized or raw
•organic
•source of coconut water
•overall flavor

So what's our verdict?

We really loved Cocozia. It isn't too sweet or too bland like other brands we have tried. It is organic so that is a big plus. There is no strange after-taste that lingers in your mouth. It is not raw, however this is the best non-raw coconut water we have ever drank. It also comes with a cute little expandable straw which is fun for kids and adults!

So how else would we use Cocozia coconut water besides drinking it straight up? Well this would be a great swap-out for the juice box in your child's lunch box. It's also a delicious liquid base for smoothies with a tropical flair.

title: Got Bunapi instead of Bunashimeji
text:
I got some cute Bunapi (white Beech mushrooms) instead of the Bunashimeji (brown Beech mushrooms) I ordered, but that's alright. The two types of mushrooms are very similar, but their nutritional profile differs with each mushroom having its strengths.

What I love about Hokto's mushrooms (they have several locally grown types including maitake, which is superb for health and cancer prevention) is that they are always clean and ready to eat -you should not wash these as they were not grown in soil nor touched by human (gloveless) hands. The company even says don't wash them. They are ready to be cut and thrown into your recipe! : ) They are always beautiful looking and taste wonderful. These are organic shrooms grown in CA by a Japanese company that is a major international player in the mushroom trade -they know what they are doing.

I don't buy them every week because they are a specialty mushroom that costs more (but that's fair). Still, I think these are great for health and people should buy and eat them as much as they can. These mushrooms could be used in anything but are wonderful in broth/pho type soups. I plan to eat in organic beef bone broth with lots of garlic and ginger -very medicinal. I will also stir fry with asparagus and tofu along with some other mushrooms. Would work great in any type of curry with beef, chicken, or tofu.

Mushrooms, in general, but especially medicinal ones deserve odes, love songs, and lots of praise. They are so wonderful. Buy these, eat them in some super yummy creative way and then go write a poem about how much you love them. : )

Kimchi, mushrooms, garlic, extra dark healthy chocolate... I love you all for keeping us all healthy! Thank you my beautiful mushrooms!

THEY GAVE ME LAXATIVES.
I guess they grabbed a ton of snacks from a Japanese pharmacy or something because some of the stuff in the picture isn't what I got. I was looking SUPER forward to trying the coca~cola candy in the picture but didn't get it.

They gave me, and this is important, an ambulance shaped packet of laxatives. It had an ambulance on it and 5 M&M candies I thought were just shaped like tiny pills as a novelty, you know? Like choco-pills. I couldn't read the Japanese language to understand it was actually laxatives...and I ate them all thinking they were just candy.

My bowels are a wreck right now, so if you do buy it, and they give you that specific thing in it? DO NOT eat the ambulance candies. They were laxatives. They will destroy your insides.

title: My kids testify, this makes the most perfect popcorn
text:
These are the secret ingredients to perfect movie theatre popcorn.

I start with refined coconut oil, maybe 3 tablespoons melted in a stir-crazy popcorn popper. Then I sprinkle the flavacol in, roughlty 3-4 teaspoons. Most of it remains in the bottom but it's super salty so this is how just enough gets on the popcorn as it's popping. I add the popcorn kernels once the flavacol has stirred around in the coconut oil.

While the popcorn pops, I put about 1/8 cup of the topping oil in a measuring glass with a spout. I heat it up for a minute in the microwave, and then when the popcorn is ready in the bowl, I slowly pour a thin stream with the spout of the measuring glass while moving the popcorn bowl around under it. Just like how the dispenser in a movie theatre works.

The popcorn comes out like an $8 bucket at the movies. Mine isn't all yellow because I use pure coconut oil without all the color additives, but the flavacol imparts a touch of color and all the nice buttery saltiness.

title: Prepare for own gift box for less
text:
My spouse bought this for me as a birthday gift. I opened the box and immediately knew what a rip off it was, so I tried to return it, but unfortunately it was ineligible, so gifter beware.

Since I was stuck with it, I figured I'd consume everything. Here's my opinion on the contents:

Sausage: one side was completely discolored upon opening it. Against my better judgement, I cut around that part and ate some anyway. It was very high in moisture (fat) content. Almost nauseating. Not impressed, but I didn't seem to get sick from it, so there's that. 1/5 stars

Candies: Sadly, the two caramel nut candies were the best thing in the box, and they were quite good. 4.5/5

Crackers: Very bland, even the garlic flavored ones. You wouldn't want to eat these on their own, and the plain ones seemed somewhat stale to me. 2/5

Cheese food: cut off a nice hunk, and almost immediately spit it out. It was that bad, and I'm not a picky eater at all. The texture was nasty, and the flavor was not much better. Maybe it would be better heated up (melted?), but I wasn't going to find out. 0/5

Infused Almonds: there were two varieties. The vanilla ones were just okay, pretty subtle flavor. Plain salted almonds are much better IMO. 2.5/5
The lemon ones were not good, almost like when you eat a bad nut. Unpleasantly pungent, and not worth the calories to me, so I tossed the rest. 0/5

Mustard: This is one of the few foods I don't care for, so I haven't tried either of them, no rating.

I honestly can't comprehend how this product had such a high rating, other than the possibility that the recipients are lying to the gift givers so as not to hurt their feelings. There are much better options if you want to send a food gift to someone, and I recommend steering clear of this overpriced pile of terrible quality, potentially unsafe food.

You could assembly your own crackers, sausage, nuts, and mustard for half the price, and you would get better quality food in a greater quantity.

Extremely dissatisfied.

title: You're missing out till you try these!
text:
These are fantastic! Usually I share all my wonderful food finds with a particular friend, but this time I'm hiding these from her because her birthday is in February and I plan on ordering her a five-pack like I ordered for myself.

Here's what's really impressing me about these. I eat really clean -- typically organic, rarely out of a box -- everything is typically cooked from scratch. I've been doing this for a number of years now so when I taste flavored coffees I don't taste flavor, I taste fake chemicals. But I used some of these in my coffee and I just get this wonderful flavor (as intense as you want to make it just by adding more). So I tried some in my water and just had a delightful taste like I had floated fruit in my water glass but I didn't have to go to the effort of cutting up the fruit.

I've tried the blueberry, strawberry, raspberry, and the french vanilla creme and have loved them all. Each really has a wonderful flavor. They came with suggestions for how much of the flavoring to use but I basically ignored that. I don't seem to need as much as some people use. But I do notice that different ones require different amounts to get the flavor I want. Oh, and what you are flavoring changes the amounts, too. So I put more in coffee than I do in water.

When I order my friend her birthday gift, I plan on getting a couple of more bottles for me -- in different flavors. I got two strawberries this time so only a total of four flavors and now I want to add a few more that would be good in coffee.

I bought this because I read that chicory root helps heal leaky gut syndrome which can cause a lot of really horrible health issues, including some that I have. I have multiple autoimmune conditions with no cures, no hope of cures in my lifetime, and I am at the end of what doctors can do to help. I got so desperate that I researched alternative treatments like diet changes and supplements and things like this because otherwise I have no more options. I don't know yet if this is helping, but I was surprised that despite the fact that I usually don't like coffee, I actually really like the taste of this stuff. I hope this helps feed the probiotics that I am consuming through food and through pills, but even if it doesn't, I am curious to try other flavors of this and I would totally get this same kind again as well. It is definitely soothing my throat when MCAS and GERD make my throat swell up. Also, you get a lot for what you pay for. title: in comparison to other non-fat dressings the Walden Farms varieties are, at best, average
text:
update: I recently left a packet of Walden Farms Salad dressing in the refrigerator overnight and, when I used the dressing the next day, I found that the dressing was much thicker than when I reviewed the dressing initially. While I didn't find the taste of the dressing to be altered much, the consistency was greatly improved.

Review of: Walden Farms Calorie Free Salad Dressing Packets- Sampler Pack

From experience I’ve decided that it is rare that any ‘calorie free’ or ‘fat free’ salad dressing fully reaches the heights in taste and texture and flavor that a ‘full-fatted’ salad dressing can reach. And, for me at least, the Walden Farms Calorie Free Salad Dressings fall into the same category. I find that they aren’t as good as their ‘full-fatted’ counterparts.

When compared against other ‘non-fat’ dressings, however, I found that the Walden brand does just an okay job of reaching the right balance between taste, thickness and ‘healthy’.

The Honey Dijon, while it was thicker than one family member expected, was at the same time a bit of a disappointment to that family member. There is no honey in the dressing but, at least it tasted sweet. However, that family member also mentioned that there was little to no taste of mustard to be had.

The Thousand Island dressing, on the other hand, was thinner than I expected. While I thought the taste was basically okay, it somewhat had that a ‘thousand island’ taste; at the same time the dressing didn’t have the texture or mouth feel of a high-quality Thousand Island’ dressing. I think I’ll use another pouch of this dressing next time as a dip; for that purpose, I think, the dressing may work better.

The Greek Lite experience was pretty much in line with the others. It was sweeter than I expected, and while it does carry a flavor that is different from the honey Dijon dressing or the thousand island dressing, it doesn’t carry along much of the ‘greek’ flavor I want.

As for the ‘Ranch flavor, I think it also falls into the ‘just okay’ category. While it was vaguely reminiscent of a Ranch dressing, it was thin and overly sweet. And, I wasn’t overly disappointed when I finished the packet.

I haven’t tried all the varieties as of yet and remain hopeful that I will find one that I consider to be a stand-out. Perhaps the Very Berry or Mango Poppy will reach that go for me; time will tell.

For now, the consensus of my family and myself is that, in comparison to other non-fat dressings that we’ve tried, the Walden Farms varieties are, at best, average. In comparison to other full-fatted dressings we’ve tried in the past, these dressing fall short.

One a high positive note, I do like the advantage of having a variety or sampler pack. Having 9 different flavors to choose from means that if one flavor doesn’t shine then I just sample another flavor. And, another great plus with this sampler pack is that the portions are small enough so if I find a flavor that I don’t care for at least I don’t have a full bottle of that flavor or for the flavors I do like, I know which flavor to order more of.

title: It'll do the job if you want cantaloupe flavored drink, it isn't quite up to Nestfruta
text:
I received as a gift a few satchels of Nestle Nestfruta melon drink from friends who brought some over from the Philippines.
I've gone to different Asian markets and cannot for the life of me find any in stock, and I was unable to order online.

I've purchased and tried Klass Mango, Horchata, Jamica, Limonado, Pina, and Coconut (purchased from WinCo).
But could never find melon in stores.
I held off on purchasing the melon variety, as the cost is more than the other drinks, but nostalgia and craving for that melon flavor got me to break down and purchase a package.

I like the flavor and color of the drink, but it doesn't hold a candle to Nesfruta. The smell after the drink is made has that hint of melon, but the powder definitely has a bit of a chemical smell to it.
The sugar granules are on the larger size and the powder does create a slight plum of powdery smoke if your an animal when scooping the drink mix, so take your time and use gentle motions when scooping into your cup.
It does take a bit longer to dissolve, so stir for a minute or so.
Mind you, I'd still get this again until I can get my hands on some Nestle Nesfruta Melon from the P.I.

text: I was so happy to see Creme Savers back after vanishing for a decade. Strawberry and creme was always my favorite so I ordered this pack of 6. The pieces are a bit smaller than they used to be. Completely understandable, MANY food products are smaller than they used to be.  Each piece is individually wrapped.  At first, the candy tastes just as it used to. But then it gets weird. Odd as this sounds, there is a burnt taste to it.  'burnt' as in burnt food.  The strawberry and creme flavor is the prominent flavor but the weird 'burnt' flavor is still there.  I had my husband try a piece and he tasted it as well. We tried pieces from 2 rolls, each had the weird taste. Maybe the flavor changed from 10 years ago? Maybe we got a bad pack of candy? Maybe it started to go bad due to the excessive heat/humidity here? (Though we did bring it inside as soon as it was delivered.) Whatever the issue, this candy doesn't taste the way it used to.  I don't think I'll purchase  Creme Savers again.  Very bummed. I was looking forward to enjoying them again.

title: A Southern Staple: Crystal Hot Sauce!
text: My dad (who grew up in New Orleans back in the 40s and 50s), always had Crystal Hot Sauce on the table when I was growing up in the 70s and 80s (still does). I didn't have any appreciation for hot sauce back then, but as I got older, I started using it on everything like the old man does... red beans and rice plus other cajun/creole dishes, burgers, po-boys, sandwiches, field greens, beans, peas, soups, dumplings, stews, pizza, popcorn... you name it! I like other mass-produced hot sauces as well, such as Louisiana brand, Frank's RedHot, Tabasco brand sauces, Tapitio brand, TryMe Cajun Sunshine, etc., but I like Crystal the best! It has a fresh, pure, cayenne pepper and vinegar bite that's always delicious with a mild, pleasant heat... and not too salty like some sauces. I also like that it has 3 simple ingredients: aged red cayenne peppers, distilled vinegar, and salt. Fortunately, I can get it almost anywhere where I live... this would be my stranded-on-a-deserted-island condiment of choice...

title: Phenomenal, but pricey, but worth it, sort of...
text:
I roast my own Sumatra Mandheling from green beans, so I think I know something about rich strong taste and high caffeine content. This Death Wish is some seriously phenomenal coffee. It's definitely the strongest tasting coffee that I have ever bought, dark and mean, full bodied with chocolate and earth tones, it most definitely has a bite to it, but it is NOT shrill or bitter, even when you overdo the grinds to water ratio. The taste is unique, unlike anything I've ever had, not like Sumatra, Kenya or other really dark roasts, it's like...its own thing.

The caffeine content is way up there, I can't say for sure whether it's more or less than what I roast at home but it's comparable, probably a lot more than mine but I can still take a nap after a cup so I'm not a good judge. If you have issues with caffeine, this is not the coffee for you. Ironically, I bought it for the caffeine content but it's the great taste that really leaves the lasting impression.

My only issue, and the reason why I gave 4 out of 5 stars, is the cost. $20 per lb. for coffee is a lot of money, sorry Death Wish. And yeah, it's not much more than $14 per lb. for Starbucks Sumatra, which is light years behind this coffee, but Starbucks is way overpriced, so that would still make this at least somewhat overpriced to me. I don't know what the market can bear or who the competition is, but I'm guessing that some people can afford to pay $20 per lb. for their regular coffee. Maybe I'm just not willing to do that, sorry. Compared to $7 per lb. of green Sumatra that I can roast to something comparable, I'll be sticking with my own roast as a mainstay, and going with this on special occasions. But I will buy it again, and again, whenever I can afford it :) Definitely worth it to anyone and everyone who does not roast their own, best dark roast, high caffeine, greatest tasting coffee available out there for purchase. Phenomenal coffee.

title: Definitely adds to juiciness without much added saltiness.
text: I mixed up an injection using the recommended ratio of 1/4 cup phosphate to 2 cups liquid. I used 1 cup reduced turkey stock (homemade) and 1 cup unsalted chicken broth (store-bought.) I injected our Thanksgiving turkey after spatchcocking it, and cooked it in a kamado grill. It was noticeably more juicy than the "test turkey" I cooked the preceding week without injecting. I did also dry-brine the Thanksgiving turkey longer, so that may also make a difference. The phosphate does add a bit of saltiness, but not as much as the same amount of salt or MSG. I'd say it would be about a quarter to a third as salty. I plan to use this for injecting poultry and pork in the future (I have Butcher's brisket injection to use for beef.) As I use the bag of phosphate up, I plan to buy another, as I am very pleased with its performance.

title: taste very natural and fresh
text:
Though the bag on this says they are good for snacking, I wouldn't recommend them for that purpose. I found that these were best used in baking as a way to infuse food with natural raspberry flavor because they are like a distillation of natural raspberry flavor packed into a small package.

They can be eaten as a snack, but you wouldn't want to eat more than one or two. The texture is crunchy and pleasant. They are naturally a little sweet and quite tart. They still have their seeds (as raspberries do) and they can get stuck in your teeth. They taste 100% of raspberry with no chemical or off flavors. It's clear that the berries that were freeze-dried were fresh with no bad spots. I wouldn't question the quality of the fruit or the process based on what was in my bag.

I used these in making a raspberry meringue by pulverizing them into a powder and adding that to the meringue mix. Because the flavor was so diluted by the meringue, it added a nice punch of flavor without adding moisture as fresh berries would. For this type of use, I found these to be more than satisfactory and would recommend them for similar uses including cakes.

We retired to South America nine years ago and there is only corn flour available, primarily for making arepas.  Wrong texture, blah taste. This year I wanted to get some cornmeal from the US and a friend visiting Texas said he’d bring me back a couple of boxes.  He couldn’t find Albers anywhere (is it not sold in Texas?) and bought a local brand.  Again, too cakey, no corn flavor, ugh.  So, I ordered two boxes of Albers on Amazon and had them brought to us by a shipping service.  It was worth the $9/pound I had to pay, there is just no substitute for Albers.

title: Blue Diamond finely-sifted is finer than other brands superfine
text:
I've bought multiple other brands of almond flour. I was usually buying Nature's Eats Superfine almond flour, simply because it was the best price and locally available. I had mistakenly assumed that all almond flour would be similar if it was super-finely sifted. When I purchased this Blue Diamond flour, I saw the finely-sifted was significantly cheaper than the Blue Diamond superfine. I went ahead and tried the finely-sifted and since I still had a little of the superfine Nature's Eats left, I was able to compare the two in texture and how grainy the flours were.
Both brands use blanched almonds. The only difference was how much they claimed to be ground. I was surprised to find Blue Diamond flour to be much more finely ground, light and powdery in a way that the Nature's Eats wasn't. Thus Nature's Eats ultimately had a far more grainy and gritty end product no matter what I used it in.
Blue Diamond finely-sifted in the 3lb bags are a really great price compared to every other brand of almond flour. I found there was no reason to pay (so much) more money for Blue Diamond's superfine because the fine-sifted was ground so well.
My only complaint is that the bag is supposed to be resealable. This brand's ziptop never seems to reseal very well at all. If that were fixed it would be great!
Very pleased, would recommend!

text:
I got this to increase my milk supply, and it was cheaper than buying the capsules. My lactation consultant recommended I take it because my baby hasn't been gaining well. It really works to increase milk supply! I went from pumping 2 ounces total to 3.5 ounces at a time, and my baby is putting on weight nicely now.
It has a same day effect: days I skip I notice less gulping from my little one. I started with 1/2 teaspoon twice a day, and now I heap the 1/2 tsp twice a day. It has an unpleasant, green tea taste and makes my mouth itch until I've washed it down, but it's worth it. It DOESN'T mix with water, and I'm off dairy, so I mash it up with a little oatmeal and then have something else as a chaser. I haven't noticed any energy effects, but I'm a chronically sleep deprived mother of an infant, so maybe it would be noticeable for someone else. I'm also taking fenugreek, which also helped some. Highly recommend.

Update:
I took this in at bedtime once and it kept me awake for three hours. Similar to how caffeine works. Lesson learned.

title: Fresh Flour Is Ground Very Very Fine!
text:
This very fresh potato flour is ground extremely fine and will be so much easier to use when thickening soups and gravies! I included some photos showing how very nicely it is milled.

When I opened the sealed, sturdy zip-close bag the flour smelled very fresh with no off-odors. The best by date for this bag is over two years in the future.

I like to keep some potato flour in the freezer to help thicken soups, stews, and gravies. This flour is ground much finer than my last purchase of another brand and will blend into the liquids faster with less chance of lumps because of that fineness. I also add some potato flour to bread recipes (when I remember) and think it keeps them a bit moister for a longer period.

According to the package, the flour is prepared in a gluten-free environment, however, the facility also processes tree nuts and peanuts important information for those with allergies to those items.

A huge bag of very nice potato flour that I can put right into the freezer without having to repackage it because the zip-close bag it comes in is heavy plastic and closes tightly.

I am a fan!

I wanted to try out Annie Chun's soup after seeing it so much at friends houses and in the stores. So I decided upon shopping one day to pick up a bowl of their Miso Soup. As far as the broth goes, surprisingly it was nice but it tastes and smells much like cheaper brands.

text: I don't know if I used these wrong, but I didn't care for them. I originally bought them to paint chocolate molds of tools for a tool box cake I made, and I was disappointed that they didn't work well on the chocolate. I do understand that this is not what they are made for, so that was probably my fault. I attached a picture of the cake. The tools on top are just colored candy melts, but the nuts and bolts on the bottom were painted with the silver, and like 5 coats of it because it just beaded up and never dried. It ended up looking kind of cool with an "old tool" look, but it wasn't what I was going for. Then I recently made sugar cookies with royal icing, and tried to use the silver and blue to color the icing. I made a pretty small batch of it in my mixer and it seemed like it took a lot of coloring to even get a light color into the icing. The blue I used turned out to be a baby blue and didn't have the metallic sparkle that a lot of the pictures show. The same with the silver, it was almost like just a pearl color and not vibrant at all. I wonder if they changed the formula or maybe I just got a bad batch. I wanted to like these and I might try to use them again, but overall I was disappointed.

title: Not their best product, that's for sure
text:
I'm a *BIG* fan of the Vitalicious VitaTop products ("maximum nutrition for minimum calories")--especially the Deep Chocolate version--so I was eager to try the BlueBran mix. But I have to say I was disappointed with this product. Don't be fooled by the photo on the box, people! The "blue bran" name is misleading--I found approximately 3 freeze-dried blueberry 'chips' in my batter. You will definitely need to add your own fresh or frozen blueberries to the mix, otherwise you'll just have plain old bran muffins.

Even after I added fresh blueberries to my batter, the end product was not very good--it was gooey and bland, with a weird after-taste. My family usually inhales the Vitalicious products, but these are still in the freezer.

I have two boxes of the mix left, so I'm going to try adding chunks of apple to the next batch, along with some cinnamon to give it some flavor, and see if I get a better result. Bottom line: Skip these and go for the Vitalicious Deep Chocolate mix.

The juice comes in a glass bottle which helps keep the juice in its natural form. The taste is a little odd but soon we got used to it.  We did not try any other brand therefore cannot speak to any differences but we do not see any issues in the product. The glass bottles are very nicely packaged in an air filled plastic packaging which protects the glass bottles very well. As for the health benefits, we both are healthy and are taking Noni juice regularly in an endeavor to boost our immune system. I in particular noticed lesser fatigue in my legs after consuming noni juice daily.  Thanks to Amazon for carrying such great products. We later order the product directly from Kannai's farm website as they carried more variants and were equally or lesser priced.

I'm not loving it, though my tastes have always run to the sour / savory side. From what I read, it's probably really good for you, but I think the trick is to treat it as food -- not medicine. If you're going to try to down 8 oz / day, you can get the same benefit from four separate servings of 2 oz each. I mixed 1 part beet/apple/ginger to 2 parts OJ, and it wasn't bad. I've certainly enjoyed other Knudsen juice products, and I trust the brand. I was lucky to be able to find this bottle at my local grocer for a couple of dollars less.

A note to the knice people at Knudsen, if they read this. Though I use a lot of ginger in my own cooking, cinnamon on beets tastes much better than ginger (or added to ginger) and, of course, on apples too.

text:
I was excited to try this brand of molasses. Someone had commented that it had a milder flavor than other blackstrap molasses. I initially agreed, but then there was a turpentine aftertaste. I'm concerned and don't feel comfortable consuming this. I would return it if I could, but there are no returns.

I am also uncomfortable with the plastic container. The molasses is hot when poured into the container making leaching of the chemicals in the plastic an issue.

Nothing on the Amazon listing nutrition facts matches with what is on the label on the container I received. Not the calories, sodium, potassium, calcium, protein, sugars and most importantly IRON! There is a 32% decrease in the amount of iron listed on the Amazon listing vs on the label on the jar I received. Ridiculous! Also, the WARNING note on the label I received says " Consuming this product can expose you to chemicals including lead and acrylamide, which are know to the State of California to cause cancer and birth defects or other reproductive harm." Of course, this warning is not part of listing on Amazon. Seems really shady! I would return this product if I could. I certainly won't be buying it in the future.

The only good thing I can say about this product is that it came intact-nothing had leaked from the container.

title: No artifical preservatives
text: I am rounding up from 4.5 stars to give it a full 5 stars due to the healthy nature of this ramen. Ramen usually is not healthy or considered so. It is after all highly processed. However, this is probably less "bad" for you compared to its competitors. It still tastes pretty decent. The shin black premium label is a sub division of Nongshim Shin, which makes really popular Korean ramen. The Korean ramen cups are a #1 best seller on Amazon and also are very popular for those who know the difference between Asian ramen and American ramen. Asian ramen comes in a wider variety of flavors than American ramen does typically. This black label premium brand is a bit more expensive than the traditional ramen cup. It is because of the fact that it does NOT use MSG.  MSG is an artificial food additive that many companies use to add a savory taste to their food without adding actual protein. While most experts debate about whether or not MSG is good or bad for you, I am reminded of the fact that any substance depending on the dose can be poison (paraphrasing Paracelsus), therefore I try to limit my intake of synthetic elements like MSG where possible.  This noodle soup has a rich broth.  It is not too spicy.  It also has ingredients that are comprehensible by many lay people. I would recommend this to others, as an alternative to regular salt-laden MSG-high ramen.

title: Flavorless and without that warm, delicious aroma one associates with cumin
text:
I use cumin a lot. If a recipe calls for a teaspoon of it, I'll ratchet it up to a tablespoon, especially with my hummus recipes. And because of that, I was excited when I received a pound of this product. But my excitement quickly went to disappointment and then to serious concern.
When opening the container the absolute absence of aroma was striking. The warm and rich smell of cumin was completely missing. One would think that a pound of cumin seed would have at least a hint of cumin. Nada! Nothing! Zip! So I I took a teaspoon of it and put it in my spice mill, hopefully eliciting something, anything, from the seeds.
After about 15 seconds of whizzing, it worked! Sort of. The faint aroma coming from my spice mill was similar to that of a very diluted paint thinner. Ummmmm.... Definitely not the result I was hoping for.
I looked more closely at the container and learned this product was "manufactured" in India! Okay, I wasn't hoping for that either.
India, similar to China, has very few laws-- if any at all -- regulating her food production.
For instance, it is true that this product may very well be 'organic' as its label states. But that merely guarantees (ahem!) that no chemicals were used during the production of the food product. In other words, human excrement could be used as fertilizer since it clearly would be organic and therefore 'legal' to use.
Why this container has the smell of paint thinner I'll never know. Perhaps the containers in which the cumin seeds are placed shared space with a solvent manufacturer. At any rate, It's going into the trash. This is a company that I will not purchase from again.
I've made it a habit of NEVER buying food products from India or China. Sadly, the origin of this cumin was not stated in the product info on Amazon.
