title: Real wild, flavor full mushrooms from the woods in Europe
text: These are some of the finest mix of wild European mushrooms you find in the woods all over Europe. I used to go with my father picking mushrooms and they tasted so good. My father would dry them too. This is a very interesting mix, some Models, Chanterels and Totentrompeten or black trumpet, my absolute favorite. Soak em in hot water covered for 30 min. Before cooking them. Use them to add a special flavor to your gravy, or marinate them slowely in a clear sauce, cutup some and serve over your rice. Or, make a simple can of cream of mushroom soup into a gourmet dish. Prepare the canned soup per instructions except reduce the liquid required by 1 cup, about 15 min into the time you are soaking a good handful of mixed mushrooms in that hot water. Drain the mushrooms and cut large pieces to bite size and add to soup, mix well than add a coup of the water the mushrooms soaked in, but run it through a fine sive. Stir, and cook on med low for 10 min or less, until the mushrooms are nice and tender, but don't overheat the soup. You can add dried spinach leaves crumbled, some diced and sweated onions, and for a real gourmet add either some canned clams washed and cut a little smaller of the bigger ones. Or, you can add corn, fresh corn cut/scrapped off a cob of corn. Taking a hamburger parddy/meat and crumble it into soup, season to taste.  Hmmmm. And double hmmmm if you use heavy cream as part or most, except for mushroom water, of the liquid needed. Now that will be a soup from heaven. BOB APPETITE!

title: Excellent quality and performance for many types of baking
text:
I’m very pleased with the quality and performance of this pastry flour. The grind level is very fine and even, and it comes packed in a traditional paper sack that’s easy to deal with. The sack was encased in a plastic pouch to contain any leakage during transit (there was none).

Pastry flour is midway between cake flour and all-purpose flour in terms of protein content. It’s a great fit for many non-yeast breads, muffins and many types of cookies. It makes for a softer texture with a finer crumb that really sets it apart from the same items made with all-purpose. It especially shines with pie crusts. You can really amp up your pie crust game with pastry flour and the use of lard. It makes the crust delicate, flaky and delicious.

In the past I’ve made my own pastry flour by blending cake flour and all-purpose. However, this designed from the start pastry flour performs much better than my ersatz pastry flour. It’s hard to find pastry flour in the store so, while this is priced well above what you’d pay for a five pound sack of all-purpose, it’s not out of line with other online sources for specialty flours. The fact that it’s organic and from family-owned farms is icing on the cake (well, pastry).

I’m very pleased with all aspects of this flour – a solid five stars.

title: Energy Drink Without The Jitters
text:
Wow! The flavors are right on the money. The blue can tastes just like blue raspberry. The red can tastes like carbonated [cherry] Robitussin (the only one I didn't like the flavor of). The yellow can tastes exactly like the flavor of a freshly cut sweet pineapple as you chew it, not a hint of tartness. And the green can tastes like classic Mountain Dew.
Nevertheless, the food coloring is so heavily saturated that you'll have to drink these sodas with clothing you don't want permanently stained.
That said, I'm not exactly sure what these drinks were designed to do but from my experience these drinks kept me wide awake without crashing afterward. I'm usually quite clumsy but under the influence of these energy drinks I had no jitters and my hand and eye coordination were spot on all day long, not a single thing in my house tipped over or dropped because of my clumsiness. It definitely came as a relief to my family when for the past week I didn't utter a single curse word. This drink was created for gamers (at least that's the impression I got from the graphics on these cans). I'm not a gamer but I am a huge fan of flavorful energy drinks - and of Mountain Dew. Whether this drink is designed for gamers or not, it definitely beats the tastes of the G Fuel lineup (even though they have way more flavors than Game Fuel). And if Faze Rug happens to read this (or fans of Faze Rug like the Rug Rat that I am), my deepest most heartfelt apology to you on my opinion.

title: No Dream and the Taste is a Nightmare
text:
Why all the sugar alcohols? Agave syrup can work just as well. It’s sweet and no aftertaste.

Anyway …

My mother has been having issues sleeping –> sometimes it is getting to sleep, then there is the staying asleep. And, I do have some “staying” asleep issues myself.

She tends to average 7-9 hours per day, I’m a 5-6 hour person. I know, I need more at my age. So, this seemed like a perfect cocktail before bed. Pop open the can, drink it down, head to bed. Great in theory.

“Naturally sweetened with monk fruit, stevia leaf, and erythritol …” – doesn’t sound like a pleasant cocktail before bed at all. Right off, for me, it had a bitter/sweet taste. Almost like medicine. I’ve had better cough syrups (still missing Vicks 44).

And, for the price which is over $2 per can – this is not a good deal. My sleep pattern didn’t improve, so I know my mother’s wouldn’t. We had better luck with ZzzQuil Ultra.

In addition, who wants to drink a whole can of stuff before bed?

Honestly, this isn’t something I’d recommend to someone. Hot tea with a bit of honey or agave would likely work better. It’d taste better too.

title: Innovative chewing gum!
text:
First I bought the smaller size container, so the fact that I'm back buying this king size one tells me I really like this gum......and I haven't chewed gum in years and years. The reason I quit chewing gum is I became concerned that the sugar in it was causing cavities in my teeth.
When I switched to sugarless, I had digestive problems so I gave up gum, until now. I don't notice any ill effects from chewing this gum, but there are positive effects. According to Web MD, "it reduces levels of decay-causing bacteria in saliva and also acts against some bacteria that cause ear infections". While I am not suggesting that you stick this gum in your ears, I am saying that sticking it in your mouth may help reduce cavities, and, in my case, it helps get me through periods of temptation in the kitchen. Instead of giving in and whipping out the chocolate, I go for this gum. It gets my mind off goodies and satisfies my craving for sweets.
There are at least three other flavors, but this is my favorite.

title: Ought to Be Illegal
text:
I think the FDA should classify these things as illegal drugs. They're so darn good that I can't even have them in the house (I haven't bought them from this vendor (and I won't comment on the price), so I'm just talking about the Golden Double Stuff Oreos, themselves). While I was binging on them, I'd force myself to eat "only" one "line" of 11 cookies a day (there are 3 convenient "lines" in each pack and that re-sealable flap on the front is great for easy access while keeping them fresh during their short existence in my vicinity). Even so, as I continued to shovel them in, I'd sit there moaning about how my liver and pancreas were hurting, my teeth and tongue were coated with fur, and my eyes were jiggling around in their sockets. Sometimes, some crumbs would fall out of my mouth while I was complaining and I'd have to root around for the errant pieces like a pig looking for truffles.

Now, given their ingredients:

"UNBLEACHED ENRICHED FLOUR (WHEAT FLOUR, NIACIN, REDUCED IRON, THIAMINE MONONITRATE [VITAMIN B1], RIBOFLAVIN [VITAMIN B2], FOLIC ACID), SUGAR, HIGH OLEIC CANOLA AND/OR PALM OIL, DEXTROSE, HIGH FRUCTOSE CORN SYRUP, CORNSTARCH, SALT, BAKING SODA, NATURAL AND ARTIFICIAL FLAVOR, SOY LECITHIN. CONTAINS WHEAT, SOY."

You might do as I did and say, "Heck, they're not that bad. After all, I can pronounce (and even recognize) most of those things." But, according to the label, the Serving Size is two (hah!) cookies. Those two cookies contain 150 calories and 7 grams of fat. Plugging that into the old Weight Watcher's point formula gives 3 points per 2 cookies. Four cookies is, essentially, a full meal. The 11 cookie "line" I was eating was the equivalent of 2/3 of my daily point allotment. Of course, with the pain in my liver and fur on my tongue, I really didn't feel any desire for any actual meals. So, I guess the points evened out in the end.

Anyway, I've banned them from the house (I've been Oreo free for maybe a month, now). I still have to force myself to not go down the cookie aisle, though. And, if I do succumb and enter the aisle, I stand there and stare at the package with a mournful, puppy-dog look on my face while I yell at myself (on the inside) to just walk away. So, I rate these at an absolutely wonderful, perfect, yummy, delicious, etc. 5 stars out of 5 and wish they were illegal. Darn, they're good. A 6-pack, hmmm....

title: Nothing Says Lovin' Like a Microwavable Brownie...Well Sorta
text:
Leave it to Betty Crocker to resuscitate the kiddie concept of the Easy Bake-Oven to produce their Warm Delights Hot Fudge Brownie. The serving size seems to remain the same child's portion as the old 1960's toy since it barely covers the bottom of the plastic bowl that contains the dry powder mix. The directions specifically state a tablespoon plus a teaspoon of water to moisten it, and knowing how temperamental baking can be, I would not try improvising this part or else you will get chocolate mush.

Forty-five seconds in the microwave and then you squeeze a packet of sugary Fudge Topping on the top. It's not bad but just seems like skimpy gratification for the 370 calories it contains, 110 of which are fat. There's also 2 grams of trans fat, 270 mg of sodium and 61 grams of cholesterol. In other words, this is not a Weight Watchers treat by any stretch. But if you are in need of a quick chocolate fix, you could do worse. As an alternative, I suggest the much tastier Fat-Free No Pudge! Brownies you can get at Trader Joe's. Without the elaborate packaging Betty Crocker seems to think is necessary for an individual serving, you can bake a dozen and then allocate them as you wish.

title: Outstanding; ignore the misguided reviews
text:
This is the best Peanut Butter product ever produced by major American food service company.

If you're expecting "peanuts and salt" with separated oil and a rock-hard refrigerated consistency after opening, this is not that product. If, however, you dislike most of those products -- which are more annoying to eat than many people find to be worthwhile -- this is what you've been waiting for.

It uses a natural tropical oil, which has a naturally long shelf-life, as opposed to the disastrously unhealthy "alternative" of hydrogenated oils.

Many people panic over seeing "saturated", but that is exactly the sort of grossly uninformative evaluation that led us to using the (far more deadly) hydrogenated oils to begin with -- advice which is frankly unforgivable. Learn about fats for yourself, and make the right decisions. I recommend "Know your fats", available right here on Amazon.

If you want the most healthy peanut butter you can get, grind your own and eat it fresh, and congratulate yourself for fantastic self-discipline and patience. For the rest of us, we need more products like this. Finally, a "grown-up" version of an American food product.

title: You have to overcook it...
text:
So if you love pasta but don't/won't/can't imbibe it as much as you'd like, this is the perfect alternative. You get veggies, protein, and fiber in one dish. Does it taste the same? Of course not - just like turkey bacon doesn't taste like bacon, but it's still good. ;) My $0.02:

1. Overcook TF out of it, period - helps a lot with texture.
2. Salt the water FFS
3. After draining it, unless you're going to consume it *all* right then (and maybe even if you are going to), drizzle light olive oil over it and toss it to prevent it turning into a giant mass

Again - you're clearly eating this because you want pasta with the stuff pasta doesn't offer (low carbs, high protein, high fiber, veggies, etc.), but be realistic: it's not traditional pasta. BUT, if you approach it correctly, it can still be tasty and you'll have 0 guilt. ;)

title: I’ve found that I can use this Avohass oil anywhere that I would normally use vegetable/olive oil
text:
Review of: Avohass New Zealand Extra Virgin Avocado Oil 16.9 Fl Oz Bottle

I’ve gone through about 1/4 of the 16.9 ounce bottle of Avohass Avocado Oil in just over a week; so, for me, I’m getting quite a lot of use out of this oil. And that use is because I’ve found that I can use this Avohass oil anywhere that I would normally use vegetable oil or olive oil.

When I first tasted the avocado oil I did notice that, in comparison to vegetable/olive oils, the avocado oil has a fundamentally different taste to it. For me, the taste is a little darker, maybe a little richer or more noticeable than other oils. But, where the difference really shines through is when the oil is heated, that heat releases the aroma of the oil so that the uniqueness of the avocado oil really shows.

I’ve been using this for sautéing vegetables, and even used the oil in an electronic pressure/slow cooker to make one of the best home-cooked versions of lima bean rice that I’ve ever made. I’ve used the Avohass Avocado oil for cooking eggs, to make popcorn, to pan fry different types of meats … the oil, for me at least, is a delicious alternative to olive oil.

I also did a quick compare of the nutritional labels between this avocado oil and some good quality olive oil and, not surprisingly, I found them similar in almost every category.

And the end-of-the-day, for me, this is a more-than-good, high quality oil just standing on it’s own, and having the oil be avocado based instead of vegetable based or oil based gives it a difference in taste that I enjoy.

title: Open one pod and be disappointed with how little coffee it contains
text:
Since I'm more interested in the jolt from a cup of coffee than staining my teeth, I've always favor either Medium or Mild (if available) roast. I've found Green Mountain Coffee K-cup so tasteless and flat that I finally decide to tear open a fresh pod to find barely a teaspoon of ground coffee in it. Nowadays, when I want the convenience of K-cup I use Kirkland Medium Coffee K-cup from Costco, and find them flavorable and strong. I've tore open the Kirkland K-cups at least twice after brewing the coffee and find the pod was packed completely full with coffee ground. I've also tried K-cups from Dunkin Donuts and found them also more superior than Green Mountain's K-cups.
As with some other reviewers, I'm also a coffee snob. I buy green coffee beans from specific regions in the world and roast them myself. You can really get spoiled this way!

title: Question: Is this edible?
text:
I can't believe I wasted so much time on a review. I deleted it all. Don't buy these. You'll just end up throwing them away. It doesn't matter how hungry you are. The amount of trash they produce is nothing but waste, of course. If these could feed some animals struggling to keep from going extinct, and that's everything but rats and roaches, by all means use reusable containers and breed those tortoises up. All tortoises native to the ... everywhere, are endangered. Everything in the oceans is suffocating on human trash and feces. This is why it takes pages. It makes me a bit mad when people sell trash as food and each bag ends up doing more harm than a grenade over the years as it floats around killing porpoises (and extincting Vaquitas, a porpoise that's gone extinct thanks to people). We could have fed them these things and maybe they could still be happily jumping around. As trash, it's not worth writing a review about. I've already deleted one. I bought them and tried. I really tried not to throw them out but I just can't eat them. I'm not picky by any stretch. These are a waste. Don't buy them. Don't bother eating them. Don't bother throwing them away. Don't bother reviewing them. It's a waste of time to return them. Every step is regrettable. So don't start it. Buy something else, if you must, but don't buy these. You will regret it, unless you're really creative. Maybe there's someone who knows a way to make these edible. See? I'm open minded. But these improvements would be miracles and they seem very far away. Do not buy.
You wouldn't believe how much I deleted. I guess I was upset. That's how bad they are.

title: Were not assembled and pieces damaged:
text:
If you purchase, buy a few days in advance in case order arrives like mine did, so you have time to plan for something else or assemble them.

The description states already assembled but what I got was NOT assembled. I'm going to have to do them all myself... It's not hard but it is time consuming and you have to be careful with the adhesives that they provide, because they are sticky and can clump, and if you mess up with those, then you won't have enough to complete the assembly.

The holes in the "e"s of the "One" cutouts were also left in (for all of them). Thankfully already perforated though, so it made it easy to remove them, but you'll want to be careful with that as well so you don't damage the "One" cutouts, since they are pretty thin.

It also arrived with 3 of the long toothpicks having something that looks like mold on them, though I guess it might not be, its just greenish/blackish, but the other toothpicks seem fine. One of the 3 with that tint also had a part chipped off.

Items Received: 4 sheets of adhesives that you use to put the pieces together (12 dabs on each sheet and you need 2 for each piece, so there's no room for error), 24 bows, 25 toothpicks (3 of them damaged), and 25 "one" cutouts.

They are cute once assembled, you just have to have the time to assemble them and be careful in the process. I like doing art and crafts but NOT happy that these did not arrive as described. If I hadn't ordered these early like I did, I would have been really upset, because it is time consuming.. As it stands, my daughter's birthday is next week, so I have some time to put these together. Had I known they would come this way though, I would have ordered them from another seller. title: This Caramel Corn Rocks!
text:
OK. The first order fulfilled by Amazon was near it's expiration date, stale and not very tasty. So we reached out to Rocky Mountain Popcorn and explained the situation to them. We didn't go through Amazon because they just wanted to do an RMA. We really just wanted the caramel corn.

Well, Rocky Mountain Popcorn really stepped up! They said they would figure out the supply chain issue with Amazon (can't have stale C-corn out there) and they dropped a replacement box of C-corn in the mail to us.

Hands down, Rocky Mountain Popcorn is the best tasting caramel corn we have ever eaten. Personally, I've eaten 'the best' C-corn in Boston, Seattle, San Fran, Philly, The Shore, and nearly every beach in the USA, and this stuff is amazing. It is a good thing it comes in manageable-sized bags, because if it was any bigger, I would be in serious trouble.

And NO....I was not paid $$$ or C-corn (I wish) for this review. This stuff is just that good. If you try it, and it's not amazing, you got a STALE bag -- it's that simple. Send it back, or take it back and get a bag with a fresh date. Don't settle for less than the best. I'm not an addict, but it may be close thing.

title: Honest Review from first time buyer
text:
First off, this was my first time trying this product. I bought the Chocolate Coconut Cookie Dough. It taste delicious and the first ingredient is Red Palm Oil, which from my research is good for your heart. There seem to be real quality ingredients in here, hence the price being more than sugary cookie doughs.

I read the reviews before mine arrived and let me just say, so many people spoke so bitterly and whined about this product being nasty and not sweet enough. It’s keto! What did you expect?

If you’re going to rip apart a company for making better for you/healthier options, then don’t even consider keto if you can’t handle not tasting overwhelming amounts of cane sugar.

The taste is light with an undertone of cherries. At first it appeared cracked on top, but if you just take your spoon and dip in, it’s soft like butter or ripe avocado. I would buy this again and recommend to others who want to stay away from harmful ingredients. They even wrote me a cute note!

(4 stars because it would be great if it was a little cheaper)

Thank you BHU foods for caring about my health!

title: Great Bars If you Don't Mind Pulling Out a Tooth or Two.... and Poo
text:
Now I'm a high energy burner semi-health nut, where I gotta eat or snack on something every couple hours... so it feels. With that said, I tend to munch of various types of energy, protein and/or whatever bars. However, I get sooooo burned out with the usual flavors... chocolate, vanilla, peanut butter, mocha, chocolate, vanilla.... you get the picture. On top of that, all these typical flavors are almost always made up of chocolate, double-chocolate or heart-attack chocolate. So I finally said, "ENOUGH!!" I don't want another frick'n "double-chocolate-cookies-n-cream-peanut-butter-infused s'mores bar" ever again!!! Well then, in comes this curious looking protein bar that claims to be made of none of that. In fact, it claims to be made of only Mango and Pineapple!?? Who does that? How do you do that?

Thus, I greedily punched that buy button as if I scored a Walmart TV on a Black Friday deal for $9.99 and then (not-so)patiently waited in front of my porch for the delivery guy to drive by and chuck it at my door without stopping. Unfortunately it didn't come that quickly, so I gave up the wait after 2 hrs and went for a few beers and yummy spicy wings.

Finally, what felt like weeks (I curse you prime member shipping!!), I got the holy grail. I smashed it open, tore into one like a rabid core-strength trainer and realized..... it smelt like strait up shi*t... or I mean, poo!!! Like WTF is this?! It couldn't have gone bad in the 2 days it took for delivery. No, no, things made from artificial poo just doesn't go bad that quickly! So I thought, ok, it must be the fact that the human nose is no longer trained to smell the goodness of real ingredients and real fruits neatly packed into a rectangular, flat insta-meal... thus the smell is now foreign and oddly recognizable as the stuff you'd find at the bottom of an outdoor port-a-potty. Wheew! Ok, glad I squeezed that one out.

So, I bit into it..... and tried with my might, with all my God-given bulging neck muscles, to pull my mouth... my head away from that gorilla glue-like substance, now stuck to half my teeth. For the life of me (and my teeth), I was fighting to retain my dentures, and all the while, I had that cliche saying in my brain on repeat... "eat or be eaten, eat or be eaten". Suffice it to say, I managed to pull away (less a chip on my front tooth), but ohhhh, the fun part just begun. On each attempt at chewing this sticky poo substance, another part of a tooth would be entangled, ensnared into the tacky, gritty "real fruit" energy bar that they called the "RXBar". I can tell you, thank goodness I didn't work out that day, cuz this wrestling match took the place. But I must say, the taste really wasn't that bad.... unless that's how poo.... um, let me not complete that thought.

In the end, I think these bars actually weren't that bad. I mean, you should see my jaw muscles. I can flex them like biceps. And my teeth? Oh, they've never been cleaner in my life. After all, I see my dentist once a week now. Siiigh, ok, back to the double-chocolate-cookies-n-cream-peanut-butter-infused s'mores bar.

title: A little goes a long way
text:
I have been using these for several years, lately on a heart diet, so I add it to my Decaf.
These are pure flavorings with NO sweetener, no fake "cream" added (so if you'd expect it to be just like a creamer, you'd be mistaken- it is unsweetened, highly concentrated flavoring). That's why you can use so little.
If you like the flavor unsweetened, use it the way it comes. If you like it sweet, add your own- I add a Stevia sweetener & skim milk.
Would use 2-3 pumps for a regular coffee cup, but my mug is 22oz, so I use 8 pumps. A bottle lasts me about 2 months.
I've tried half a dozen flavors, but do have a couple favorites. It's worth it to me to be able to customize my Decaf to my taste.

text:
I read some of the other reviews about how much less cheese these puffs had--someone goes so far as to suggest the ones ordered through Amazon are the least cheesy. (And he meant that in a bad way...)

Since I had just ordered a box, I was a bit nervous. Perhaps they weren't as good as I remembered...perhaps the quality had gone downhill. It happens.

And the box arrived and I opened a bag and was practically buried in delicious white cheddar cheese. If anything, the quality was BETTER than I remembered. Not just chock-full-of-cheese, but baked perfectly and completely free of grease. Not painfully crunchy. Just perfect.

These are wheat and gluten free, too...which makes me believe I could go gluten free...as long as I had Michael Seasons White Cheddar Cheese Puffs by my side.

Hell, I could win a war with these babies by my side.

Okay, that's a bit of an exaggeration. But that's how they make me feel. Truthiness.

Yum.

title: Had to Try It!
text:
A retro TV channel I follow on social media posted an article about Cactus Cooler. I had never heard of Cactus Cooler and learned it came about from The Flintstones cartoon. My husband never heard of it either. People were leaving all kinds of comments on the social media post about the drink and how much they loved it (and still do) as a child. I looked it up, found some on Amazon and placed my order. Couldn't resist! It arrived the very next day. I was so excited to try it but had to pop it in the fridge first. Finally, it was cold enough to try. I'm not the biggest fan of orange flavor so I didn't except to be blown away by CC. To my surprise, I enjoy it! I expected it to be super, sugary sweet. And it IS sweet, but not sickeningly sweet...at least not for me. I can taste both the orange and the pineapple flavors. Everyone in the family tried some and really enjoyed it.

I'm thinking of crushing some ice and blending a can of CC into a slushie. Perfect for a hot, summer day.

I normally would NEVER spend so much money for 6 cans of soda but I was curious and wanted to try Cactus Cooler, so no complaints there. As for buying it again, I have no plans to. But that's due to the fact I'm weaning myself entirely off of ALL soda. Never say never.

title: Even my picky husband LOVES these
text:
We love these cheddar bread/biscuits. My husband compares them to Red Lobsters 'cheddar bay biscuits'...not sure if that is exactly true as its been probably 10 years since I last tried them, but they are dang good.

We like a sharp cheddar cheese in them best. Quick and easy to make (that is a big selling point too!). The texture is a bit different then regular bread, but it is by far one of our favorites in the GF land. The outside gets a bit crispy, the inside is soft and fluffy with a slight chew. The chewiness is what separates it from regular bread, but that is something we love about it. Great as a side for soups and stews.

So yes, this is not a gluten bread replica, but its one of the few GF options we have ever tried that actually gets tender and fluffy. Love Chebe bread.

The plants themselves arrived bare-root, wrapped in moist moss (the same that came in the packaging along with the pot). They gave clear planting instructions and tips on how to successfully grow the venus fly traps.

I was very impressed with this, and my little guys are currently thriving. :) They were both the same size, and I was worried they both wouldn't fit into the pot, but they both fit in the pot and there was plenty of leftover moss and room.

Overall, Joel's Carnivorous Plants delivered with exceptional plants, instructions, and customer service. If I ever want another carnivorous plant, I'd definitely go here in the future.

title: Excellent papadum
text: I recently discovered that I need to adhere to a gluten-free diet.  As a result, the only affordable prepared product that delivers that great "crunchy, munchy" snack texture were potato chips.  Yet to my surprise, papadum are 100% gluten-free.  They deliver that wonderful crackly texture we gluten-free folks crave, except with far more flavor than a traditional cracker.  Best of all, they're very easy to prepare!  I just lightly spritz both sides with spray/aerosol oil, wipe it around to evenly coat, and microwave for no longer than 20 seconds.  It perfectly replicates the same deep-fried flavor and texture of the papadum I've enjoyed at Indian restaurants since a very young age (but with much less fat).  I particularly enjoyed the intense spice of the Punjabi Masala, and look forward to sampling the other flavors as well!

title: Very cool way to play with cocktail mixology!
text:
I purchased this to make what I called "Gravity cocktails" to bring as a themed drink to an Oscars party last weekend. The kit looked challenging so I decided to try them out the night before to troubleshoot the process before the big event (and glad that I did). Overall, the process was very straightforward and simple (if you follow the directions), however it is a somewhat lengthy process with a few steps to follow and probably about an hour of prep time - so probably better for a dinner party or something where everyone can either participate or watch as the caviar is made, rather than something to rely on for the signature drink of your event.

There are 3 recipes included in the kite and we tried out the cosmo martini version with the little caviar bits (and plan to try the other 2 - foam and encapsulation - another time.) Due to the amount of time it took to create the little "caviar" bubbles for the drink, I ended up making some in advance the day of the Oscars party and bringing them in a Tupperware container to add to the cocktails, rather than trying to make the caviar at the party.

During the trial process the night before the party, my friend took pictures as we went along and then posted them to her blog along with tips & tricks that may come in handy if you decide to try this kit, her blog can be found here: [...]
Overall, the product was exactly as described and worked surprisingly well - we had fun making the caviar (they are really cool once you're finished and add a great texture and wow factor to the cocktail) and we're for sure looking forward to trying out the mojito version of the kit this summer! :)

title: Reasonably Intense Great Flavor
text:
Review of Aiello Caffe Italian Espresso Intenso Coffee Beans, Medium Roasted Whole Bean Coffee Blend, 2.2 Pound Bag sold by International Loft DBA Authenticico.

I lack the experience to verify that this is an authentic Italiano espresso. I used this for espresso in both my semi-automatic espresso machine and a single test brew in a moka pot. The flavor was great.

I brewed solely as an espresso and not as regular coffee. I use a stainless steel pitcher instead of glass to collect the brew so at first the crema looked a little lacking but tested a brew into a glass pitcher and the crema was very nice and a little denser than what I had been noticing with my daily espresso blend.

The flavor was great, especially as a change from my daily routine. Had been using a medium espresso roast (Cuban-style) for my daily latte to switching to this provided a greater impression of intensity that I might otherwise have not noticed as much.

I screwed up and tossed the empty bag so I cannot list any information about Best By or Roasting dates but recall that the Best By date was probably in the order of 7 to 9 months.

A rating for "giftable" was left blank as a bag of espresso beans is not my idea of a great gift.

title: Good item, just add veggies! Recommend.
text:
This review is for the Hormel Complete "Swedish Meetballs", it is a really good item!

As usual, I always need more than just this meal, though if you have a roll or a price of bread (1-2) , you could add it and that would be great.

I usually like to add a half a can of veggies!

This meal, is a prepackaged meal which makes it easier for those who can not cook or if you are to busy to cook. It is also great for a go-bag. Incase of an emergency.

This meal is precooked, which is amazing.
I love that! All you just need to do is just pop it into the microwave for a few and you have yourself a nice hot meal, even if you do not have anything to add to it.

A great shelf stable food for you.

A great item for the elderly.

A great item for a teenager, who can't cook.

Perfect for someone who is disabled.

Also, great for those with depression.
(They may be to depressed to cook but "know" they must eat.)

I personally am a single mother with autism, raising an Autistic daughter and I do not currently have a stove (but I also don't really know how to cook either), but these meals are a way that we can have a nice home-cooked meal. Both myself and my daughter can easily make these.

The Flavor: Good, my daughter likes it alot. I personally don't care for it as much (but everybody's taste-buds are different).
(To me personally it is alright but I like the roast-beef and mashed potatoes, with salt & pepper and veggies, either peas, carrots and peas, or corn, sometimes green beans.)

The freshness: Well, it is a prepackaged food. It is actually good.

Value: I actually did not mind the price at all, I normally wouldn't pay that much for meal but I love that it is pre cooked.

I also like how long the meal lasts, before it expires. That I like!

I also like how I can toss a few into out Bug-Out-Bags and warm it up wherever I am going.

It is a nice comfort food to have,
It is filling and Shelf Stable!

title: How do you get that milk tea flavor?!  Recipe pleease!
text:
I'm at a complete loss as to how this product has any good reviews.

The package does not come with any instructions, but I figured "3 in 1" means that all I needed to do was add water. Not only did I try water; I made a batch using milk, then another batch using almond milk. I've used as much as 6 spoons of this powder for 2 cups (16 oz) of fluid. I barely noticed any flavor at all. I added sugar; still didn't get that taro milk tea flavor I certainly am over paying for ($3.75 for 16 oz!) at my local bubble tea store. Yet, I'm still at a loss at how the store pulls it off.

I heat the milk in a pan, add the powder, never allowing it to come to a boil, then chill in the refrigerator. I'd be willing to re-rate this product if I knew how to get it right! Tonight, I'm going to try adding a few earl grey tea bags to see if it does the trick, but as of now, I really can't taste the "taro".

UPDATE: I went to 4-5 boba tea shops and found that this powder actually tastes very similar to the taro tea that's available in most of my local boba tea shops (there are dozens located in the Atlanta area). My favorite shop simply uses a different and completely unknown recipe that sets the bar very high. I've upgraded my 1 star rating to 3 stars for those who want a cheap and good standard way of making this at home.

title: Pure honey
text:
I use honey as a treatment, b/c I have ulcer. It helps me a lot to treat my wounds. Also, that’s delicious. I would recommend it.

Add this on February 22, after ordering 2 more.

People are talking about dark color, strong taste, and crystallizing, so I provided some information. I hope help you too.

The aroma and flavor of honey, as well as its color, are in accordance with the plant from which the bee has provided nectar. In different regions, honey is obtained with different concentrations, and this difference cannot be a determining factor to identify the quality of honey; For example, honeys that are obtained in humid areas, mostly have a low concentration. In contrast to the honeys obtained from mountainous areas, it has a high concentration. The color of honey also depends on the type of nectar that the bee collects, and it varies from very light yellow to dark red and even black. Also, the geographical area and weather conditions are effective in determining the color of honey, so the color of honey, like its concentration, cannot be a determining factor for identifying the quality of honey.

Dark Honey:
Different types of dark honey from thyme, fir, oak, buckwheat and wild flower honey have a dark color. They have high nutritional value. Dark honey has a dark brown or dark amber color. Dark honey usually has a strong and spicy taste compared to light honey. Dark honey contains a high concentration of antioxidants and other nutrients.

In general, it has seven color ranges:
1. watery white
2. bright white
3. white
4. Very light amber
5. light amber
6. amber
7. dark amber

Why does honey crystallize?
Bees also add a type of diastase enzyme called invertase to the nectar, which together with sugar and starch substances that make up four fifths of the nectar's weight, are the main factors in the crystallization of honey, and the speed of this process is directly related to the ratio of carbohydrates, that is, the ratio of fructose and glucose, is directly dependent on the type of flower and vegetation and the season of honey harvesting in the region, which means that the crystallization of honey is also different depending on the type of flower. For example, cotton, rapeseed, and sunflower honeys are among the honeys that crystallize and solidify within a period of less than a month, while acacia honey take longer.

How to prevent honey from crystallizing?

Why do you want to avoid this? You are going to disrupt a natural process in natural honey. Natural honey normally forms clay or crystallizes. But if for any reason you want this to happen, we suggest the following ways.

One of the effective factors to prevent sugaring of honey is increasing the humidity of the environment. If you keep natural honey in a place that has a lot of moisture, the possibility of it becoming crystallized will be greatly reduced. In general, the higher the humidity of the environment, the slower the natural honey will turn to sugar.

Note that putting honey in the freezer or heating honey to prevent sugaring is not very correct and may cause damage to natural honey. As soon as you keep the honey at a temperature away from 10 to 20 degrees Celsius, the possibility of honey becoming sugary is greatly reduced.
The End.

title: Love These -- Nice change!
text:
I was very wary of this bar because I had KIND's savory bars and was less than impressed by them. However, these are so much better to me. Whereas those seemed inherently wrong, like having a tuna fish ice cream sandwich, these seemed perfectly balanced. Instead of being some weirdly sweet-and-savory collaboration, this was more like a thick cracker.

This flavor reminds me of hummus -- the texture is slightly crunchy, but you can taste the starchy creaminess of the beans. It's very herby, a little peppery, and it has a slight spice that builds in the back of your throat. I like my foods over-herbed and spiced, so some people may think that it's too much. They are a little neater to eat than the Nature Valley bars. There's some crumbling, but not a lot.

I like to keep snack bars and granola bars in my desk in case of emergencies and/or to keep me satiated through out the day. However, most healthy snack bars and packaged snack options are sweet -- all have dried fruit, chocolate glazed nuts, peanut butter, etc. It gets tiring. This was refreshing...and delicious!

title: Not even close!
text:
I bought this thinking it would be nice to eat a spaghetti that was gluten free and not expensive. I bought a few packages because I always follow the package directions first, then I play with it if it's not to my liking.

Attempt 1 was like eating a gummy spaghetti noodle with a nasty after taste. I had to add sauce and butter to kill the taste.

Attempt 2 wasn't any better. It was still gummy and gluey like and the flavor wasn't very good either.

Attempt 3 was a little better in that the water didn't look like a gelatin style mess when we drained it but the noodles were chewy and I couldn't finish the second bite.

Attempt 4 was when I finally said no more "pasta joy". I ended up trying to cook it by breaking the noodles in half first, thinking maybe it just isn't that great for cooking as long noodles. Oh no. I ended up having to take out clumps of noodles, tear them apart from each other and put them back in the pot. I gave up towards the end and just threw the clumps of noodles out. The texture was slimy, gummy and sticky and the aftertaste is still like pet food.

If you are used to over cooked spaghetti drowned in sauce, I could see how this would be great... But if you want something that tastes and acts like spaghetti, this is NOT it.

I can't figure out how this got 5 stars. It was horrible in taste and texture and was nothing close to spaghetti. I bought Hodgkins Mills rice and flaxseed noodles and they are perfect in texture and taste. But I won't buy pasta joy again.

title: The absolute best popcorn available!
text: This popcorn is every bit as good as you can imagine. I've never been a huge popcorn fan, but this particular brand and type of popcorn is truly addictive. The popcorn is smaller than regular popcorn and much more tender without the tough hulls. It also pops much easier on the stove. Follow the simple directions on the package and it pops perfectly every time. This is the best popcorn you'll ever have, and it won't have the hulls and tough pieces that get stuck in your teeth or in your throat. Give it a try, it is absolutely worth every cent.

title: Best stevia I have ever had!
text:
If you have ever used stevia and been dismayed by the bitter taste? Join the club. Some add ingredients to help this situation but then you have to add more to get the level of sweetness you want. What if you were able to have pure stevia in your coffee, lemonade, tea without the aftertaste? What if it were from a small bottle that lasts and lasts? This is exactly what you get with Stevia Select. All of what is said about the use of stevia is true of this brand more so than others. That a little goes a long way and once dissolved, there is none of that bitterness. This is the only brand I will be using from now on!
Thanks to Peter and Diana for this amazing product!

title: Phenomenal texture and flavor; will be enjoying again and again!

Needless to say, I anticipate more Vegan is Believin' Mac & Cheese in our future. Enjoy!

title: Yummy!
text:
I’ve always liked Hearts of Palm. When I saw the package of it shredded, I had to try it. I tasted it first. I liked it. But I didn’t know how it would be with just sauce on it. This is like the same predicament as spaghetti squash. It’s just not starchy enough.
Since I’m not on Keto or any other diet (but should be...HA!), I really wanted to
give it a try. So I cooked 1/2 the amount of pasta I usually make & when it was partially cooked, I added the Hearts of Palm into the pot, in about the same equivalent as the spaghetti would be when cooked al dente. I made sure to thoroughly mix the pasta & H of P together with a fork, as it cooked. (It was actually hard to tell the difference between the spaghetti pasta & the Hearts of Palm pasta! When done, I drained as usual & added to my sauce. All I could say was, “It’s divine!!!”
The next time I make spaghetti, I think I’m going to try a larger percentage of the Hearts of Palm pasta. I found it very interesting how good the combination of the two were & how it seemed to be mostly spaghetti pasta with a hint of the Hearts of Palm taste & texture. The reason I want to try a 1/3 spaghetti pasta to 2/3s Hearts of Palm combo is to see if it still seems like mostly spaghetti pasta...and, because I actually liked the Hearts of Palm combo better than plain spaghetti pasta! I really did! It was that little bit of interesting texture & flavor that I really liked. It didn’t overshadow the spaghetti pasta, but added something wonderful to it! I’ll let you know how it was, after I try it. Until then, I may try some other ways to use this new way of eating an old favorite of mine!

title: A Soft And Subtle Flavored Seasoning That Didn't Really Remind Me Of Kimchi
text: When I first saw Kimchi Go 100% Kimchi Origin Seasoning I had expectations for a bold seasoning mix that would remind me of kimchi. The 3.17oz bottle has a dual dispenser top holding a fine orange powder seasoning blend. One side allows you to shake the seasoning out while the other is a larger opening that allows you to pour out a larger amount or fit a 1/4 teaspoon into this space. The seasoning has an appealing aroma and is easy to add to plain flour to create a coating for oven fried chicken or to top or add to cooked foods as a finishing touch. I had added it to ramen, directly on top of fried eggs, and as a finishing touch to pan fried fish. Surprisingly, the flavor is mild and subtle and despite including chili pepper powder was barely spicy in heat. The label is written almost entirely in Korean, thankfully I was able to find information regarding ingredients and the nutritional label on their Amazon product page. The ingredients include Freeze Dried Powder (Cabbage, Chili Pepper Powder, Radish, Garlic, Ginger, Onion, Sugar, Sea Salt, Salted Anchovies, Salted Shrimp, Chives, Fish Stock, Fructooligosaccharide), Clove, Chili Pepper Powder, Ginseng Flavor Powder, Stevia, and Shiitake Mushroom Powder. This product contains seafood (salted anchovies, salted shrimp, and fish stock), if you have a seafood allergy, please be aware. When it comes to the nutritional label, there is 1765mg of Sodium, 57g Total Carbohydrate, and 17g Protein. I was unable to determine how much kimchi seasoning is included in one serving. The product that I received has a best by date of 16 months from the date that I received it. Overall, it is a fine seasoning but frankly it is too mild for me.

title: Tasted old, almost spoiled
text:
So, these weirdly arrive in a what looks like a little zippered clear travel case (make up bag?) kind of thing, that is not airtight at all, although the sticks are each vacuum packed, of course. Just seems pretty excessive in terms of packaging, in this day and age of a lot of companies trying to offer a smaller enviro footprint.

I was getting the Smokewood fatty sticks, for the longest time, now being on the keto diet, and unfortunately I guess those are so popular that the demand is exceeding supply, because they aren't offered through subscribe and save anymore. Because a keto and healthy ingredient friendly meat snack has become a staple, I like a product that can just be delivered monthly, which is why I opted to try these, once the Smokewood product was no longer an option.

This is a skinnier stick, and tougher skinned, although the meat itself is somewhat soft. Kind of reminds me of a Slim Jim. I appreciate the ingredients, but, for me, the flavor was just objectionable. It looked and tasted old, almost to the point of tasting nearly spoiled, with a bitter, just "off" taste to it. The meat stick was also quite dark, inside and at the ends, as opposed to most meat sticks that keep a more ruddy color.

The freshness date was fine, and the stick packaging had no tears or pinholes. No mold was evident, so, I guess it's just in how they process the meat and seasoning. It just did not have a fresh, meaty taste. The texture was also not inviting. The skin doesn't chew easily, and the meat has a somewhat grainy feel, in the mouth.

So, I'm sorry to say that these just didn't do it for me. I guess I will track down the Sweetwood product and order direct from them, as I see they are certainly still in business. Not sure why Amazon can't keep them in stock, but I guess it's because I'm not alone in finding them to be the best keto meat stick being made.

This one really fell short. I won't be ordering again.

I do applaud the great ingredients, and the price point is certainly laudable. I just don't like the taste, sadly.

title: Very, very weak
text:
What is this stuff--highly concentrated water??? It's useless!

For reference, if I'm using real sugar to sweeten a single cup of tea, I would use exactly two teaspoons to get the perfect taste. Two. Freaking. Teaspoons. This "concentrated" stevia syrup took around four times that to do anything at all. I say "around" because I put it in an eyedropper bottle for ease of use and it took OVER EIGHT FULL EYEDROPPERS to make even a slight difference. Keep in mind that, out of frustration, I had stopped counting after six, so the total could be much higher, AND that I eventually combined it with a different brand of stevia sweetener before it finally worked.

Part of me wants to say that it's my taste buds' fault and I'm too used to a lot of sugar, blah blah blah, but c'mon! Two teaspoons ain't a whole lot, and a concentrated SYRUP should at least be able to equal that! And then there's the other brand of stevia that I used that did a far better job with just a few drops! What other conclusion can I come to except that this stuff is useless???

Not impressed. Their eyedropper bottles are great (the one I tried, anyway), but these? Save your money. For me, I'll try finding other uses for it to avoid waste and consider it a $20 lesson well learned. Although, do consider trying those eyedropper bottles because, like I said, THOSE are great. This stuff is a massive waste.

title: A Good Choice for Himalayan Pink Salt
text:
My wife and I keep seeing this kind of salt show up on TV cooking shows and because we cook everyday, we wanted to try it. When we saw this available for review from VINE, we agreed.

First of all, we need to stress that reviews of food products are pretty much matters of personal taste. We are giving this product 5 stars because it's reasonably priced, similar to what we see in our local grocery stores, and because the grinder works well for us. To have some of this salt in your spice cabinet, this is a good choice.

Having said that, we honestly can't tell any difference in taste from regular salt. Perhaps you will be able to distinguish a distinctive flavor here, but our palate concluded: This is salt.

Also, having seen this salt used in cooking shows, we were envisioning it might have an aesthetic value, adding something like a dash of pink color to a dish. In fact, we tried it in several applications, and we could barely see the salt. I guess if someone wanted to dump a whole lot of it on the food, it would be more visible, but we have to be honest and say: We couldn't distinguish an aesthetic advantage here.

So, we're giving it 5 stars because it is, indeed, precisely what it promises.
If you want to have this ingredient in your spice cabinet, it's a great choice.

title: Deceptive Packaging
text: Natierra offers ORGANIC freeze-dried blueberries in almost identical packaging. Blueberries are close to essential for brain health and cognitive resilience. However, blueberries that are not "organic" are cultivated with massive amounts of pesticides resulting in a very different crop from blueberries cultivated with no chemical or toxic additives. The Natierra packaging for both "organic" and not organic blueberries is so close to identical that you might-- as I did here-- purchase the non-organic blueberries by mistake. Are they good (tasty)? They're okay. Do they provide nutrition? Probably. Is this a good price? Well, for a product that is not "organic", perhaps. Do you feel okay about eating them? Not really. Pay a few dollars more and buy the organic version. Ethically, Natierra should change the packaging to avoid hoodwinking customers.

text:
*I technically received the Noodle Lover’s Box as a gift. But seeing as it’s basically the same as the variety set (minus the chopsticks), I‘ll just put my review here.

I have never heard Momofuku before, but from what little research I’ve done, they are a high-end restaurant chain.

The noodles themselves are pretty good. They have a nice texture and are a decent quality. There is a problem, however, with there not being enough sauce provided to keep the noodles moist. They get tacky and sticky when you follow the cooking instructions that’s shown on the packs.

As for the sauces, the only flavors I’ve tried so far are Soy and Scallion and Tingly Chili. And they taste exactly like what their names imply. One tastes like soy sauce with scallions and the other, chili sauce (personally I have to add sweet chili sauce because the chili sauce alone just tastes spicy with no flavor. And it does tone down the spiciness, but that’s a personal problem for me).

It shocks me to see how much these noodles cost. Almost $50 for 15 packs of bland tasting noodles? Yeah, no. You’d be better off buying your own plain noodles and ingredients to create your own sauces. I’m sorry, these just aren’t worth that kind of money, even if they are supposedly from a fancy chain restaurant.

title: Best Salt there is.
text:
Update: November 2018

This is the only salt we use, and it is incredible. The flavor profile of this salt has completely changed the way we approach our use of it.

One thing to note: this product is Unrefined. It says so multiple times on the bag, in the product description, and through the marketing. It's something the company is very proud of. If you are looking for a lab made, chemically perfect, bleach white salt- this product is Not For You. If however, you are interested in Real salt straight out of the ground where a sea used to be thousands of years ago in the middle of Utah... Well then my friend, you need look no further. :)

As always, I would recommend to add your salt (and other seasonings) While Cooking so they can benefit from the heat.
______________
April 2017
Purchased this at the recommendation of Megan Gilmore, as mentioned in her Detox cookbooks. I am just shocked at how different it tastes. We have been off iodized salt for years now and after doing sea salt for a while we'd switched to kosher salt because of Alton Brown. (lol- so many opinions) We'd also picked up a grinder of pink Himilayan salt at some point- and Himilayan tastes bland compared to this stuff.

It's just So different. It's very mild, so I do find myself using a bit more than I generally would. With other types of salt using more would come with a side of swelling for me though, and that hasn't been happening with this salt.

I would highly recommend this. Also, I didn't realize it when I bought this, but it's a 2 pack.

title: ABSOLUTELY NO FLAVOR ON ANYTHING, BAD SELER!
text:
This product has a tremendous flavor when you try it from the shaker, BUT it lacks any flavor past that. I smoked a pork butt with it SLATHERED in this rub, and it looked amazing to only be let down with ABSOLUTELY no flavor at all. I was embarrassed to serve it to everyone at my weekly Sunday dinner party. Everyone including myself are in total agreement that it had no flavor whatsoever.

Moving forward I decided to try it on some just grilled chicken the next day. I again coated the chicken so heavy it would have to hold flavor, YET IT DID NOT! It looked amazing, and had not a single shred of flavor to it. Not even an ounce of flavor. I took the remaining grilled chicken to work as a blind taste test to my fellows managers, and not to my surprise they asked me if I put anything on it, because it SEVERELY LACKED FLAVOR AT ALL. Most went on to say that it just tasted like bland grilled chicken. So I wasn’t crazy.

Moving forward I reached out to the seller thinking I may have gotten a bad batch of this seasoning after reading some of the reviews citing the same issues. I got absolutely no response from them at all. So in turn I will not be buying anymore of this tasteless dry rub, and will definitely be avoiding the seller at all costs, due to no communication at all. I would STRONGLY SUGGEST anyone reading this to stay away from this seller and dry rub. If you want to try it anyway I will do you a huge solid, buy it, open the box, throw it away, and go either smoke your meat or grill without the dry rub on it, say it lacks all flavor, and it will literally be the same experience as using the rub heavily coated on it. You’re welcome.

title: YUM!  DELICIOUS!
text:
BROOKLYN BEANS DECAF VARIETY PACK SINGLE CUP COFFEES

Under doctor's orders, my hubby may only enjoy decaf coffee. Believe me when I tell you that he has tried EVERY brand out there -- we even have two coffee makers on the counter -- his and hers. I still go for my high powered java, but Tom has really grown to enjoy decaf. When we saw this variety pack of k-cups, direct from Brooklyn, New York -- well, how could we go wrong?

This handy package comes with 40 cups. There are eight different flavors and five each of those flavors. The enticing coffee blends are -

Cinnamon Subway
Coney Island Caramel
Maple Sleigh
Hazelnut
Brooklyn Bridge Blend -- Medium Roast
Breakfast Blend -- Light Roast
Vanilla Skyline
Fuhgeddaboutit -- Dark Roast

The names are a riot but the tastes are divine. So far, Tom has tried the Vanilla Skyline and Fuhgeddaboutit cups and liked both of them very much. These cups are Keurig compatible and that includes the 2.0 Keurig cup brewers. The price is right, the coffee is rich and full of flavor, you get a large variety, and only 100% Arabica coffee beans are used. Plus, this decaf coffee does not have the yuck, bland, cardboardy taste of so many other decaf brands. Hurrah!

Also, the box they come in is made of very sturdy cardboard and is very interesting, made up with pictures of Brooklyn, a handy area wherein you can tear to open and even keep the coffee cups right in the box. There is a introduction blurb from the three guys in Brooklyn who love coffee and are responsible for this great decaf coffee and have formed the Brooklyn Bean Roastery. It is very hard and unusual to find GOOD tasting DECAF coffee, but we have found some that I know I will keep purchasing for my hubby.

Also included inside the box is a card with two points -- happy? and unhappy? If you are happy with their product, the Brooklyn Bean Roastery is happy! However, if you are unhappy, the card states -- "If you're not happy, we're not happy! But please, let us help! If for some reason you were absolutely unsatisfied with the Brooklyn Bean product you received, please contact us and we will make it up to you." How about that for service - ?

But with this rich and wonderful tasting coffee, how could you be unhappy? We are very pleased customers!

text: This cereal is not quite as hearty as some muesli I am used to, but is excellent. Many characteristics on the plus side: is truly multigrain (contains wheat, oat, corn, rice, barley and millet), is sweetened only just enough to appeal to the palate - which is to say it is not horribly sweet like the common American breakfast cereal, is light and crispy with some of the ingredients powdery so they tend to combine with milk and make it thicker, and does in fact have a nice light blueberry flavor. The only aspect I'm not thrilled about is that the raisins and almonds are scarce compared to the excellent, less expensive muesli-type cereal I buy at the local Aldi. This Nature's Path cereal has a corn-flake-like chip predominant, as shown on the box.

title: Know what you are buying -- read carefully.  This is Turmeric Lemongrass, NOT Chai
text: They need to either rename this tea, or give the listing another title, because it's very confusing.  This is the Turmeric, Ginger, and Lemongrass variety.  If you are looking for Turmeric Chai, so you can make golden milk or a turmeric latte on the stove, this is NOT it.  You instead need the Turmeric Pepper variety.  This tea is mostly lemongrass and ginger, with chai spices, and a little turmeric sprinkled throughout.  It is very tasty though, so I gave it 4 stars despite it NOT being what I wanted to buy.  That's my fault, because I was going by the name and not the ingredients, and I didn't know until AFTER I'd made my purchase that the actual Turmeric Chai was sold under another name.  Buy this tea if you want a very spicy, lemony, warming beverage.  There's no way it can stand up to milk though and made in a pot on the stove the traditional way...it doesn't have nearly enough turmeric in it for that.  If you're reading this Vahdam...rename this to Turmeric Lemongrass.  It's more accurate and less confusing.

title: A Nice Surprise
text:
I took a fair amount of ribbing from friends for ordering a "$10 bottle of soy sauce". I figured you only live once. And since we buy these three-pound bags of Mandu potstickers at Costco, we're always in the hunt for a new dipping sauce.
Most are variations of a theme...soy, with either ginger, garlic, or sesame dominant.
This sauce offers no such clues, even down to its consistency...seemingly as much a delicious glaze as a dipping sauce.
In any case, the taste is fantastic as is the whole flavor experience, as much for its uniqueness as its wonderful flavors. You never go, "it's a sweet sauce, or its a hot sauce"...you go this is a deliciously melded sauce of undefined origin.
Glad we took a chance. He who dares wins !

title: CarbSport Mixed Berry
text:
CarbSport Mixed Berry drink is one of the better ones that I have tried. I have been riding/racing road and mountain bikes for 10+ years and tried all the major brands. Starting with the taste, is it a berry drink and goes down smooth, it does finish with a slight film but not bad. The directions say to use 1-3 scoops per bottle, I have settled on 1-1.5 scoops, this is all I can handle as far as the flavor is concerned. Now keep in mind I will dilute Gatorade because I think it is “too strong/concentrated” so my preference is just that. It does completely dissolve leaving no residue in the bottom of the bottle, which is a MAJOR plus for me. There are others out there that feel like drinking sand at the bottom of the bottle, but not this one.
When it comes to the effectiveness of it, I don’t have a concrete “it works” but so far I do like it. I have used it after a snack and on an empty stomach it settles great. Since it is winter, I have don’t any on bike comparisons, but at the gym doing weights then spin class so far so good, I will continue to use it and see how the rest of the container feels. Once it warms up enough to ride out side again I’ll add an on bike section and I see if it helps me with a cramping issue that I have been trying to figure out.
At this point I would definitely recommend trying CarbSport Mixed Berry.

title: Solid Cacao Nibs
text:
Good cacao nibs. Give you that great deep bitterness like from dark chocolate and has a pleasant crunch. Packaging is solid and well sealed so no issues there.

Cacao nibs are UNSWEETENED and basically unprocessed so don't expect the smoothness or sweetness of actual chocolate.

Excellent on yogurt or in baked goods!
